Câu 12

a. Customer: Excuse me, how much is this jacket?

b. Shop assistant: It’s 500,000 dong.

c. Customer: That’s a bit expensive. Do you have a cheaper one?

Câu 13

a. Mai: Would you like to join our school football team?

b. Nam: I’d love to, but I’m not very good.

c. Mai: Don’t worry. We practise twice a week.

d. Nam: Okay, I’ll give it a try.

Câu 14

Dear Peter,

a. I’m sorry I haven’t written for a long time.

b. I have been busy preparing for my final exams.

c. They will finish next week, and then I’ll have more free time.

d. Write back soon.

Love, Linh

Câu 15

a. The tiger is now one of the most endangered animals in Asia.

b. Habitat loss is the main reason for this decline.

c. Moreover, illegal hunting continues in some regions.

d. Protecting forests is therefore essential to save the species.

Câu 16

a. Therefore, many schools now encourage students to read for pleasure.

b. Reading regularly improves vocabulary and concentration.

c. It also helps students to relax after a busy day.

d. Despite these benefits, fewer teenagers read books today.

exercises.passage:
English Speaking Club

Do you want to improve your English? Come and join our club! We meet 17 Friday afternoon in Room 12.

The club was set up two years ago by a group of teachers who noticed that numerous students understood grammar well but felt too shy to speak. Our friendly atmosphere is designed to help everyone overcome that fear step by step.

What do we do?

Members practise speaking 18 games, role plays and group discussions. Our teacher, who comes from Canada, 19 everyone to speak without fear of making mistakes.

Why join us?

You will make friends, build confidence and 20 your pronunciation. The club is free, and new members are 21 welcome. Contact Ms Hoa 22 more information.

Each session ends with a short feedback round in which members share what they have learned. There are no exams or marks, so you can relax, make mistakes and enjoy using English with classmates who share your goals.

exercises.title: Câu 23–32 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 23–32).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Online learning has grown rapidly, especially since schools around the world were forced to close during recent years. [II] Millions of students discovered that lessons could be delivered through video calls and learning platforms. [III] Many of them have continued to use these tools even after returning to classrooms. [IV]

2One of the main advantages is flexibility. Learners can study at their own pace, review difficult parts of a lesson and choose the time that suits them best. In addition, online courses give students in remote areas access to teachers and materials that would otherwise be out of reach.

3However, online learning is not perfect. Without a teacher present, some students lose motivation or become easily distracted. Others do not have a stable internet connection or a suitable device, which makes it challenging for them to take part. Social interaction, which is crucial for emotional development, is also limited.

4Numerous educators therefore support “blended learning”, a combination of classroom and online activities. This approach keeps the personal contact of traditional lessons while using technology to make them more engaging. With careful planning, it may become the standard model of education in the future.

(Adapted from an education report)
exercises.tr: Học trực tuyến phát triển nhanh; linh hoạt, tiếp cận được vùng xa nhưng thiếu động lực, hạ tầng và tương tác; mô hình kết hợp có thể là hướng đi.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 33–40).
exercises.passage:
1Sports play an important role in the life of students. Besides keeping the body strong, they teach young people valuable lessons such as discipline, cooperation and respect for rules.

2In team sports like football and volleyball, players learn that success depends on everyone working together. Even an excellent player cannot win a match alone. Moreover, losing a game can teach students to handle disappointment and to try again, a skill that is useful in every part of life.

3Unfortunately, numerous schools give sports a low priority. Pupils sit for hours in classrooms and have few chances to exercise. This lifestyle is linked to health problems such as obesity and back pain. Some experts therefore recommend at least one hour of physical activity every day.

4Parents can also encourage children by joining them in activities like swimming or cycling at weekends. In this way, sport becomes a happy habit rather than a duty.

(Adapted from an education journal)
exercises.tr: Thể thao rèn thể lực, kỷ luật, hợp tác; nhiều trường xem nhẹ, học sinh ít vận động; chuyên gia khuyên mỗi ngày ít nhất một giờ; phụ huynh nên đồng hành.

exercises.title: Câu 1–5 · Sắp xếp câu
exercises.instruction: Chọn phương án sắp xếp các câu/lời thoại thành một đoạn hội thoại hoặc đoạn văn hợp lý (câu 1–5).
exercises.passage:
Câu 1

a. Proponents of remote work contend that eliminating the daily commute frees up hours that employees can devote to family and rest.

b. Critics, however, point out that the boundary between professional and private life tends to dissolve when the kitchen table doubles as an office.

c. The pandemic compelled thousands of companies to experiment with working from home on a scale that had previously seemed unthinkable.

d. Whether the arrangement endures will therefore depend less on technology than on how organisations redefine productivity and trust.

e. Once the initial emergency had passed, many firms discovered that output had not declined as they had feared.

Câu 2

a. Mai: I’d rather not go to the concert if it’s going to rain.

b. Tom: According to the forecast, the showers should clear up by the evening.

c. Mai: In that case, count me in.

Câu 3

Dear Ms Harrington,

a. In view of this, I would be grateful if you could consider extending the submission deadline by one week.

b. I am writing to request an extension for my dissertation proposal, which is currently due on 14 March.

c. A prolonged illness during February prevented me from accessing the university library and meeting my supervisor.

d. I have attached a medical certificate confirming the dates of my absence.

e. Thank you for your time and understanding; I look forward to your reply.

Yours sincerely, Linh Tran

Câu 4

a. Receptionist: Certainly, sir. Would you prefer a room overlooking the garden or the sea?

b. Guest: Good evening. I’d like to book a double room for three nights, please.

c. Guest: The sea view, if it isn’t too much extra.

d. Receptionist: It’s only an additional ten dollars a night, and breakfast is included.

e. Guest: Splendid. Then I’ll take it.

Câu 5

a. Thanks to these combined measures, the species, once on the brink of extinction, now numbers more than five hundred individuals.

b. In the 1970s, hunting and habitat loss had reduced the population of the Amur tiger to fewer than fifty animals.

c. Even so, conservationists warn that the recovery remains fragile, since poaching has by no means disappeared.

d. Alarmed by the decline, Russia introduced strict legislation and established several protected reserves.

e. In addition, joint patrols with local communities have made illegal logging and hunting far harder to carry out.

items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    c – e – a – b – d — đúng · c (đại dịch buộc công ty thử làm việc từ xa) → e (khi khủng hoảng qua đi, họ nhận ra năng suất không giảm) → a (ủng hộ) → b (Critics, however: phản biện) → d (therefore: kết luận).
  • B
    e – c – a – b – d — sai · e cần đại từ/ý đã nêu trước (“initial emergency”) nên không thể mở đầu
  • C
    c – a – e – b – d — sai · a đặt trước e làm “Critics, however” không còn đối lập với ý ngay trước
  • D
    a – c – e – d – b — sai · b và d đặt cuối sai: d mới là kết luận (therefore)
💡 Mở bài nêu bối cảnh → diễn biến → quan điểm ủng hộ → phản biện (however) → kết luận (therefore).

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    b – a – c — sai · b không thể mở đầu vì thiếu ngữ cảnh “the forecast” trả lời cho điều gì
  • B
    a – b – c — đúng · a nêu lo ngại về mưa → b trả lời theo dự báo → c “In that case” chốt quyết định đi.
  • C
    a – c – b — sai · “In that case” (c) phải đứng sau thông tin mới của b
  • D
    c – b – a — sai · c không thể mở đầu hội thoại
💡 “In that case” luôn đi sau một thông tin điều kiện.

✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    c – b – a – d – e — sai · c mở đầu ngay sau lời chào mà chưa nêu mục đích thư
  • B
    b – a – c – d – e — sai · a có “In view of this” nên không thể đứng ngay sau b khi chưa có lý do
  • C
    b – c – a – d – e — đúng · b nêu mục đích thư → c nêu lý do → a “In view of this” đưa ra đề nghị (this = lý do ở c) → d đính kèm bằng chứng → e cảm ơn.
  • D
    b – c – d – a – e — sai · d (đính kèm) đứng trước lời đề nghị làm “In view of this” mất nghĩa
💡 Thư trang trọng: mục đích → lý do → đề nghị → tài liệu đính kèm → cảm ơn.

✔ Đáp án đúng: D
  • A
    a – b – c – d – e — sai · a “Certainly, sir” trả lời yêu cầu nên không thể đứng trước b
  • B
    b – a – d – c – e — sai · d trả lời “too much extra” ở c nên không thể đứng trước c
  • C
    b – c – a – d – e — sai · c trả lời câu hỏi của a nên không thể đứng trước a
  • D
    b – a – c – d – e — đúng · b yêu cầu đặt phòng → a hỏi lựa chọn hướng phòng → c chọn sea view → d giá thêm → e chốt.

✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    b – d – a – e – c — sai · a nói “these combined measures” nên phải đứng sau cả d và e
  • B
    d – b – e – a – c — sai · d (“Alarmed by the decline”) cần b trước để có “the decline”
  • C
    b – d – e – a – c — đúng · b (suy giảm) → d (alarmed by the decline: ban hành luật) → e (In addition: bổ sung biện pháp) → a (these combined measures: tổng hợp kết quả) → c (Even so: cảnh báo).
  • D
    b – e – d – a – c — sai · e có “In addition” nên không thể đứng trước biện pháp đầu tiên là d
💡 “these combined measures” = tổng hợp các biện pháp đã nêu → phải xuất hiện sau chúng.

exercises.title: Câu 6–10 · Điền từ vào đoạn
exercises.instruction: Đọc đoạn văn rồi chọn phương án phù hợp nhất cho từng chỗ trống đánh số (câu 6–10).
exercises.passage:
The notion that human beings are rational decision-makers has long underpinned classical economics. Yet behavioural research has repeatedly shown that, when confronted with complex choices, 6. Rather than weighing every available option, people tend to rely on mental shortcuts, 7.

One such shortcut is the anchoring effect: the first figure we encounter, however arbitrary, exerts a disproportionate influence on later judgements. Retailers exploit this tendency by displaying an inflated “original” price beside the discounted one, 8.

It would be mistaken, though, to dismiss these shortcuts as mere flaws. In everyday life they enable us to act swiftly when time is short, 9. The real danger arises only when a heuristic is applied in circumstances for which it was never suited. 10, consumers who understand how their own minds work are far better placed to resist manipulation.

(Adapted from a behavioural economics textbook)

opts: people frequently act in ways that deviate systematically from theoretical predictions
theoretical predictions are frequently deviated systematically by people
it is systematically deviating from theory that people frequently act
deviating systematically from theoretical predictions, people’s acts frequently
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    people frequently act in ways that deviate systematically from theoretical predictions — đúng · Chủ ngữ “people” + động từ “act” phù hợp, đối với “deviate from”; cấu trúc chủ động, rõ nghĩa.
  • B
    theoretical predictions are frequently deviated systematically by people — sai · bị động “deviated … by people” sai vì “deviate” là nội động từ
  • C
    it is systematically deviating from theory that people frequently act — sai · cấu trúc chẻ “it is … that” bị lệch động từ
  • D
    deviating systematically from theoretical predictions, people’s acts frequently — sai · mệnh đề rút gọn bị treo (dangling) vì chủ ngữ không phải “people’s acts”

✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    what psychologists call heuristics — sai · “what” không đứng sau dấu phẩy để bổ nghĩa cho danh từ
  • B
    that psychologists call them heuristics — sai · “that” không dùng sau dấu phẩy, lại thừa đại từ “them”
  • C
    which psychologists term heuristics — đúng · Mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định “which psychologists term heuristics” bổ nghĩa cho cả “mental shortcuts”.
  • D
    psychologists calling them heuristics — sai · V-ing “calling” bị treo vì chủ ngữ không khớp

opts: which persuade shoppers that a bargain is being offered
thereby persuading shoppers that they are getting a bargain
so persuading shoppers that they are getting a bargain
to be persuaded shoppers that they are getting a bargain
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    which persuade shoppers that a bargain is being offered — sai · “which persuade” sai chia động từ (which = hành động displaying → persuades)
  • B
    thereby persuading shoppers that they are getting a bargain — đúng · “thereby + V-ing” chỉ kết quả của hành động ở mệnh đề chính.
  • C
    so persuading shoppers that they are getting a bargain — sai · “so + V-ing” sai cấu trúc
  • D
    to be persuaded shoppers that they are getting a bargain — sai · “to be persuaded shoppers” sai bị động

opts: and which in many cases lead to perfectly adequate decisions
and in many cases leading to perfectly adequate decisions
and in many cases they lead to perfectly adequate decisions
in many cases it leads to perfectly adequate decisions
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    and which in many cases lead to perfectly adequate decisions — sai · “and which” làm câu thiếu mệnh đề chính
  • B
    and in many cases leading to perfectly adequate decisions — sai · “and … leading” không song song với “enable”
  • C
    and in many cases they lead to perfectly adequate decisions — đúng · Hai mệnh đề độc lập nối bằng “and”: “they enable… and in many cases they lead…” — song song, đủ chủ ngữ.
  • D
    in many cases it leads to perfectly adequate decisions — sai · thiếu liên từ nối hai mệnh đề, “it” sai chủ ngữ

✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Consequently — đúng · Câu trước: heuristic chỉ nguy hiểm khi dùng sai hoàn cảnh → Consequently: vì vậy, người hiểu tâm trí mình sẽ chống lại thao túng tốt hơn.
  • B
    Conversely — sai · Conversely: chỉ mối quan hệ đối lập, không có ở đây
  • C
    Nevertheless — sai · Nevertheless: nhượng bộ, không hợp mạch nguyên nhân – kết quả
  • D
    Admittedly — sai · Admittedly: thừa nhận, không phải kết luận

exercises.title: Câu 11–20 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 11–20).
exercises.passage:
1Over the past two decades, cities from New York to Singapore have invested heavily in parks, green roofs and restored waterfronts. Such projects are routinely celebrated as unqualified goods: they filter pollution, temper summer heat and offer residents a refuge from the relentless pace of urban life. Yet a growing body of research suggests that these benefits are not always shared equally, and that the very improvements meant to enhance quality of life may displace the people they were designed to serve.

2The mechanism is deceptively simple. When a neglected district acquires a new park, the surrounding land becomes more desirable, and property values climb accordingly. Landlords, anticipating higher returns, raise rents; developers, eager to capitalise on the trend, replace modest housing with upmarket apartments. Long-standing residents, whose incomes seldom keep pace with such increases, find themselves priced out of the very neighbourhood that has just been beautified. Researchers have dubbed this phenomenon “green gentrification”.

3Evidence from Barcelona is instructive. [I] A study of more than a hundred newly created green spaces found that rents within a few hundred metres rose markedly faster than in comparable areas without them. [II] Planners had generally assumed that residents of poorer districts, having the least access to nature, would reap the largest gains. [III] The data pointed the other way: the steepest increases occurred in precisely those districts that were already struggling with affordability. [IV] Those most in need of cleaner air and open space were often the first to be forced out.

4Cities are not helpless, however. Several have begun to pair greening schemes with protective measures, such as rent stabilisation, community land trusts and mandatory quotas for affordable housing in new developments. Critics counter that such policies are costly and politically contentious, and that they risk discouraging the very investment that makes parks possible. Advocates reply that the alternative — improving a neighbourhood only to empty it of its original inhabitants — is a form of environmental injustice that no municipality should be willing to tolerate.

5What emerges, then, is not an argument against urban greenery but a plea for foresight. A park is never merely a patch of grass; it is an intervention in a local economy, and its consequences extend well beyond the boundaries of its fence. Planners who treat equity as an afterthought risk building cities that are greener, yet no fairer, than those they replace.

(Adapted from an urban studies journal)
exercises.tr: Công viên và không gian xanh làm tăng giá thuê nhà, đẩy cư dân thu nhập thấp ra khỏi khu vực (green gentrification); ví dụ Barcelona; các thành phố đang thử biện pháp bảo vệ nhưng còn tranh cãi; cần nhìn xa và công bằng khi quy hoạch.

items.q: The word “temper” in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ____________.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    moderate — đúng · “temper” (v) = làm dịu, làm giảm nhẹ ≈ moderate.
  • B
    intensify — sai · intensify = làm tăng, trái nghĩa
  • C
    disguise — sai · disguise = che giấu
  • D
    provoke — sai · provoke = khiêu khích

items.q: According to paragraph 1, what does a growing body of research suggest about urban green projects?
opts: Their advantages may not reach all residents equally.
They have failed to reduce urban pollution.
They are celebrated only in Asian cities.
They are deliberately designed to displace poorer residents.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Their advantages may not reach all residents equally. — đúng · Câu cuối đoạn 1: “these benefits are not always shared equally”.
  • B
    They have failed to reduce urban pollution. — sai · Đoạn 1 nói chúng “filter pollution”, không thất bại
  • C
    They are celebrated only in Asian cities. — sai · “from New York to Singapore” — không chỉ châu Á
  • D
    They are deliberately designed to displace poorer residents. — sai · Chúng được thiết kế để phục vụ cư dân, không phải để đẩy họ đi

items.q: Which of the following is NOT implied in paragraph 2?
opts: Developers may replace cheaper homes with more expensive ones.
Landlords expect higher returns once an area becomes attractive.
Rising prices can force established residents to leave.
Long-standing residents usually benefit from the income growth that follows a new park.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: D
  • A
    Developers may replace cheaper homes with more expensive ones. — sai · Ngụ ý đúng: nhà phát triển thay nhà bình dân bằng căn hộ cao cấp
  • B
    Landlords expect higher returns once an area becomes attractive. — sai · Ngụ ý đúng: chủ nhà tăng giá vì kỳ vọng lợi nhuận
  • C
    Rising prices can force established residents to leave. — sai · Ngụ ý đúng: “priced out”
  • D
    Long-standing residents usually benefit from the income growth that follows a new park. — đúng · Đoạn 2 nói thu nhập của cư dân lâu năm “seldom keep pace” với giá tăng — không hề hưởng lợi từ tăng thu nhập.
💡 Câu NOT/EXCEPT: gạch ba đáp án đúng, chọn cái trái với bài.

items.q:
Where in paragraph 3 does the following sentence best fit?
This assumption turned out to be badly mistaken.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    [I] — sai · [I]: chưa có giả định nào để “this assumption” quy chiếu
  • B
    [II] — sai · [II]: đứng trước câu nêu giả định
  • C
    [III] — đúng · “This assumption” = giả định của các nhà quy hoạch (câu liền trước [III]); câu sau là dữ liệu cho thấy điều ngược lại.
  • D
    [IV] — sai · [IV]: cách xa câu nêu giả định, mạch bị đứt

items.q: Which of the following best summarises paragraph 3?
opts: The Barcelona study showed rents rising fastest in the districts least able to afford them, contrary to planners’ expectations.
Barcelona’s planners successfully predicted which districts would gain the most from new parks.
Rents rose equally in areas with and without new green spaces.
Poorer districts in Barcelona gained the most from the new parks.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    The Barcelona study showed rents rising fastest in the districts least able to afford them, contrary to planners’ expectations. — đúng · Ý chính đoạn 3: khu vực khó khăn bị tăng giá nhiều nhất, ngược dự đoán.
  • B
    Barcelona’s planners successfully predicted which districts would gain the most from new parks. — sai · Trái ngược: planners đã dự đoán sai
  • C
    Rents rose equally in areas with and without new green spaces. — sai · Trái ngược: tăng nhanh hơn ở khu có công viên
  • D
    Poorer districts in Barcelona gained the most from the new parks. — sai · Trái ngược với nội dung đoạn

items.q: The word “they” in paragraph 4 refers to ____________.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    several cities — sai · Không phải chủ ngữ của “risk discouraging”
  • B
    such policies — đúng · “Critics counter that such policies are costly… and that they risk discouraging…” — “they” = such policies.
  • C
    critics — sai · Critics là người phản đối, không phải chủ thể “risk”
  • D
    new developments — sai · Không hợp nghĩa

items.q: Which of the following can be concluded from paragraph 4?
opts: Protective measures are universally accepted as practical.
Opinion is divided over whether the cost of protecting residents is justified.
Municipalities have unanimously adopted rent controls.
Critics believe that parks should never be built.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    Protective measures are universally accepted as practical. — sai · “universally accepted” — quá tuyệt đối, đoạn nêu có chỉ trích
  • B
    Opinion is divided over whether the cost of protecting residents is justified. — đúng · Đoạn 4 trình bày hai phía: critics (tốn kém) vs advocates (bất công).
  • C
    Municipalities have unanimously adopted rent controls. — sai · “unanimously” — chỉ “several” cities
  • D
    Critics believe that parks should never be built. — sai · Critics chỉ lo chi phí, không phản đối công viên

items.q: Which of the following is TRUE according to the passage?
opts: Green gentrification can occur even when a project is intended to benefit existing residents.
The Barcelona study excluded districts struggling with affordability.
All planners correctly predicted that residents would be displaced.
Community land trusts have solved the problem in most cities.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Green gentrification can occur even when a project is intended to benefit existing residents. — đúng · Đoạn 1 và 3: dự án nhằm phục vụ cư dân vẫn có thể đẩy họ đi.
  • B
    The Barcelona study excluded districts struggling with affordability. — sai · Ngược lại: chính các khu khó khăn có mức tăng lớn nhất
  • C
    All planners correctly predicted that residents would be displaced. — sai · “Planners had generally assumed” ngược lại
  • D
    Community land trusts have solved the problem in most cities. — sai · Bài không nói đã giải quyết được phần lớn

items.q: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
opts: Greening schemes that ignore their effect on housing may end up harming the very group they were meant to help.
Parks should be avoided in low-income districts.
Environmental benefits and social fairness cannot be achieved together.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Greening schemes that ignore their effect on housing may end up harming the very group they were meant to help. — đúng · Suy ra từ toàn bài: nếu không tính tác động nhà ở, người nghèo có thể là người chịu thiệt.
  • B
    Parks should be avoided in low-income districts. — sai · Quá mức: bài không đề nghị tránh công viên
  • C
    Rent stabilisation always discourages investment. — sai · “always” — quá tuyệt đối, chỉ là lo ngại của critics
  • D
    Environmental benefits and social fairness cannot be achieved together. — sai · Bài cho rằng có thể kết hợp bằng chính sách bảo vệ
💡 Bẫy suy luận: từ tuyệt đối (always, never, cannot) thường sai.

items.q: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
opts: Green Spaces, Hidden Costs: When Urban Improvement Prices Out the Poor
Why Cities Should Stop Building Parks
Barcelona: A Model of Equitable Planning
The Economic Benefits of Urban Gardens
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Green Spaces, Hidden Costs: When Urban Improvement Prices Out the Poor — đúng · Bao quát cả hiện tượng, cơ chế, bằng chứng và giải pháp.
  • B
    Why Cities Should Stop Building Parks — sai · Bài không phản đối xây công viên
  • C
    Barcelona: A Model of Equitable Planning — sai · Barcelona chỉ là ví dụ, và là ví dụ tiêu cực
  • D
    The Economic Benefits of Urban Gardens — sai · Chỉ nói lợi ích kinh tế là lệch trọng tâm

exercises.title: Câu 21–28 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 21–28).
exercises.passage:
1For decades, secondary schools across the developed world have begun lessons at an hour that suits administrators rather than adolescents. Teenagers’ internal clocks, however, shift markedly at puberty, making it biologically difficult for many to fall asleep before eleven at night. Compelled to wake at six, they accumulate a chronic deficit that no weekend lie-in can fully repay.

2When a school district in Minnesota postponed its start time by an hour and a half, the results startled even sceptics. Attendance improved, car accidents involving young drivers fell, and teachers reported that pupils were more alert during morning classes. Yet the gains in test scores were modest, a finding that opponents were quick to seize upon. Researchers cautioned that attributing every improvement to sleep alone would be unwise, since other factors were changing simultaneously.

3Opponents raise practical objections as well. Later finishing times collide with sports fixtures and part-time jobs, while working parents, whose own schedules cannot be shifted, face the daunting prospect of supervising teenagers in the early hours. Some schools have responded by offering supervised study sessions, but these cost money that few budgets can spare.

4Nevertheless, the weight of evidence suggests that the benefits extend beyond academic results. Adequate sleep is associated with improved mental health, and schools that tolerate sleep deprivation may be paying for it in other ways. The question, therefore, is not whether teenagers need more sleep, but whether society is prepared to rearrange its routines in order to provide it.

(Adapted from an education policy review)
exercises.tr: Giờ vào học sớm trái với đồng hồ sinh học của thanh thiếu niên; thử nghiệm ở Minnesota cải thiện chuyên cần và an toàn nhưng điểm số tăng ít; có trở ngại thực tế; vấn đề là xã hội có sẵn sàng thay đổi nhịp sinh hoạt hay không.

items.q: In paragraph 1, the writer is ____________.
opts: criticising schools for putting convenience before adolescents’ biological needs
praising administrators for choosing sensible start times
arguing that weekend lie-ins fully solve the problem
denying that teenagers’ body clocks change at puberty
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    criticising schools for putting convenience before adolescents’ biological needs — đúng · Câu đầu: giờ học phù hợp quản lý hơn thanh thiếu niên; sau đó nêu cơ sở sinh học.
  • B
    praising administrators for choosing sensible start times — sai · Ngược giọng điệu phê phán
  • C

exercises.passage:
Câu 1

a. Defenders of the technology counter that every artistic revolution, from photography to digital editing, was initially dismissed as a threat to genuine craftsmanship.

b. Generative software can now produce paintings, melodies and even short stories in a matter of seconds.

c. Nevertheless, there remains a fundamental difference between a tool that assists human imagination and a system that imitates it wholesale.

d. This achievement has alarmed illustrators and composers, who fear that their livelihoods will be undercut by machines trained on their own work.

e. Whether society accepts that distinction will shape copyright law for decades to come.

Câu 2

a. Lan: Would you mind lending me your notes from Monday’s lecture?

b. Huy: Not at all, as long as you return them before the exam.

c. Lan: Of course. I’ll scan them tonight and give the originals back tomorrow.

Câu 3

Dear Mr Okafor,

a. Having studied the job description carefully, I am convinced that my background in community outreach suits the role.

b. I am writing to apply for the position of Project Coordinator advertised on your website on 3 June.

c. My curriculum vitae, which is enclosed, provides further details of my qualifications and references.

d. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application with you at your earliest convenience.

e. In particular, I have managed several environmental campaigns during the past four years, involving over two hundred volunteers.

Yours sincerely, Hoa Nguyen

Câu 4

a. Passenger: Good morning. I’d like to check in for the flight to Osaka.

b. Agent: Certainly. May I see your passport and booking reference, please?

c. Passenger: Here you are. Could I possibly have a window seat?

d. Agent: I’m afraid those are all taken, but I can offer you an aisle seat near the front.

e. Passenger: That’ll do nicely, thank you.

Câu 5

a. Consequently, many of the island’s beaches now remain deserted during the very months when visitors once flocked there.

b. Then rising sea temperatures bleached large areas of the reef.

c. Local operators, however, are beginning to promote inland attractions such as forest trails and cooking classes.

d. Divers have long regarded the island’s coral reef as its principal attraction and contribute most of its tourism revenue.

e. Finding the underwater scenery drab, divers have taken their business elsewhere.

Every notification that lights up a phone screen represents a small victory in the competition for human attention. exercises.title: Câu 11–20 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 11–20).
exercises.passage:
1For much of the twentieth century, mending a broken appliance was a mundane domestic skill rather than an act of rebellion. A toaster that failed was taken to a local shop, and a torn coat was stitched by a neighbour. Today, however, such repairs are increasingly obstructed by sealed casings, proprietary screws and software that refuses to function once a non-approved part is installed. Campaigners argue that these practices are not accidental but deliberate, designed to push consumers towards replacement rather than repair.

2The consequences are considerable. Electronic waste is now the fastest-growing category of refuse worldwide, much of it consisting of devices that could have been restored at a fraction of the cost of a new purchase. Manufacturers, for their part, insist that restrictions protect safety and intellectual property, and that amateur repairs may endanger users. Yet independent studies have found little evidence that authorised repair is meaningfully safer than competent repair by third parties.

3Legislators have started to take notice. [I] In 2021, France introduced a “repairability index” that obliges sellers to display a score indicating how easily a product can be fixed. [II] Early results suggest that the label has influenced purchasing decisions, since many shoppers now treat a low score as a warning sign. [III] Several American states have gone further, passing laws that compel manufacturers to supply spare parts and diagnostic tools to independent workshops. [IV] The European Union is preparing comparable legislation that would apply across all member states.

4Sceptics caution that mandatory repairability could raise prices, since designing durable, modular products costs more than assembling sealed ones. They also warn that rules drafted by politicians are likely to lag behind rapidly evolving technology. Proponents respond that longer-lasting goods save households money over time and that the true price of disposable design is simply passed on to the environment, where it is paid by everyone.

5Perhaps the most striking development, however, is cultural rather than legal. Community “repair cafés”, where volunteers help strangers revive broken lamps and laptops, have spread to thousands of towns. Participants say the experience teaches them not only practical skills but also a different relationship with possessions, one based on stewardship rather than disposal.

(Adapted from a consumer affairs magazine)
exercises.tr: Việc sửa chữa đồ dùng bị cản trở bởi thiết kế kín; rác điện tử tăng nhanh; Pháp, một số bang Mỹ và EU ban hành luật “quyền sửa chữa”; hoài nghi về giá cả; phong trào repair café thay đổi cách nhìn về đồ vật.

items.q: The word “obstructed” in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ____________.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    hindered — đúng · obstruct = cản trở ≈ hinder.
  • B
    assisted — sai · assist = giúp đỡ, trái nghĩa
  • C
    ignored — sai · ignore = phớt lờ
  • D
    permitted — sai · permit = cho phép, trái nghĩa

items.q: According to paragraph 1, campaigners believe that restrictions on repair ____________.
opts: are intentionally designed to encourage replacement
were common in the early twentieth century
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    are intentionally designed to encourage replacement — đúng · “deliberate, designed to push consumers towards replacement”.
  • B
    result mainly from safety regulations — sai · An toàn là lý do của nhà sản xuất (đoạn 2)
  • C
    were common in the early twentieth century — sai · Đầu thế kỷ XX sửa chữa rất phổ biến
  • D
    occur only in electronic devices — sai · Bài nêu cả quần áo, nhưng nhấn mạnh thiết bị

items.q: Which of the following is NOT true according to paragraph 2?
opts: Electronic waste is the fastest-growing category of refuse.
Manufacturers claim that restrictions protect safety.
Independent studies found authorised repair to be significantly safer.
Many discarded devices could have been restored cheaply.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    Electronic waste is the fastest-growing category of refuse. — sai · Đúng theo đoạn 2
  • B
    Manufacturers claim that restrictions protect safety. — sai · Đúng theo đoạn 2
  • C
    Independent studies found authorised repair to be significantly safer. — đúng · Đoạn 2: nghiên cứu độc lập “little evidence” rằng sửa chính hãng an toàn hơn đáng kể.
  • D
    Many discarded devices could have been restored cheaply. — sai · Đúng theo đoạn 2
💡 NOT true = trái với bài; đối chiếu từng đáp án với đoạn được chỉ định.

items.q:
Where in paragraph 3 does the following sentence best fit?
Companies, in turn, have begun to redesign their products to score better.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    [I] — sai · [I]: chưa có điểm số/ảnh hưởng đến người mua nên chưa có “in turn”
  • B
    [II] — sai · [II]: đứng trước câu nêu tác động đến người mua
  • C
    [III] — đúng · Nối tiếp ý người mua coi điểm thấp là dấu hiệu xấu ([II]) → “in turn” công ty cải tiến sản phẩm.
  • D
    [IV] — sai · [IV]: lạc đề, câu liền kề nói về luật EU

items.q: Which of the following best summarises paragraph 3?
opts: Governments in France, the United States and the European Union have begun legislating to make products easier to repair.
France’s repairability index has failed to change shoppers’ behaviour.
American laws on spare parts were later repealed.
The European Union is waiting for France to finish its legislation.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Governments in France, the United States and the European Union have begun legislating to make products easier to repair. — đúng · Đoạn 3 liệt kê các biện pháp lập pháp ở Pháp, Mỹ, EU.
  • B
    France’s repairability index has failed to change shoppers’ behaviour. — sai · Ngược nội dung: chỉ số có ảnh hưởng
  • C
    American laws on spare parts were later repealed. — sai · Bài không nhắc bãi bỏ
  • D
    The European Union is waiting for France to finish its legislation. — sai · Bài không nói EU chờ Pháp

items.q: The word “They” in paragraph 4 refers to ____________.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Sceptics — đúng · “Sceptics caution… They also warn…” — They = Sceptics.
  • B
    products — sai · products là tân ngữ, không thể “warn”
  • C
    politicians — sai · politicians chỉ là người soạn luật
  • D
    households — sai · households là đối tượng ở câu sau

items.q: Which of the following can be concluded from paragraph 4?
opts: Supporters of repair legislation believe the apparent savings of disposable design are illusory.
Critics have proved that repair rules raise prices.
Politicians usually understand technology better than manufacturers.
Durable goods are unaffordable for most households.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Supporters of repair legislation believe the apparent savings of disposable design are illusory. — đúng · Proponents: giá thật của thiết kế dùng một lần “is simply passed on to the environment”.
  • B
    Critics have proved that repair rules raise prices. — sai · “have proved” — quá mức, chỉ “caution”
  • C
    Politicians usually understand technology better than manufacturers. — sai · Bài nói luật “lag behind”, không so sánh
  • D
    Durable goods are unaffordable for most households. — sai · Bài nói hàng bền giúp tiết kiệm tiền

items.q: Which of the following is TRUE according to the passage?
opts: Several American states require manufacturers to supply parts and tools to independent workshops.
France’s index applies to all goods sold in Europe.
Repair cafés charge participants for lessons.
Manufacturers admit that restrictions are unnecessary.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Several American states require manufacturers to supply parts and tools to independent workshops. — đúng · Đoạn 3: “compel manufacturers to supply spare parts and diagnostic tools”.
  • B
    France’s index applies to all goods sold in Europe. — sai · Chỉ nói Pháp, không nói toàn châu Âu
  • C
    Repair cafés charge participants for lessons. — sai · Bài không nhắc phí
  • D
    Manufacturers admit that restrictions are unnecessary. — sai · Nhà sản xuất khẳng định cần hạn chế

items.q: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
opts: The repair movement reflects a change in attitudes towards possessions as well as in the law.
Repair cafés will soon replace manufacturers’ workshops.
Legislation has already eliminated electronic waste.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    The repair movement reflects a change in attitudes towards possessions as well as in the law. — đúng · Đoạn cuối nêu thay đổi văn hoá bên cạnh luật pháp.
  • B
    Repair cafés will soon replace manufacturers’ workshops. — sai · “soon replace” — suy diễn thiếu căn cứ
  • C
    Legislation has already eliminated electronic waste. — sai · “eliminated” — trái với đoạn 2
  • D
    Most consumers prefer sealed devices. — sai · Bài không đề cập

items.q: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
opts: Fixing the Throwaway Culture: The Rise of the Right to Repair
France Leads Europe in Electronics Manufacturing
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Fixing the Throwaway Culture: The Rise of the Right to Repair — đúng · Bao quát vấn đề, luật, tranh luận và văn hoá sửa chữa.
  • B
    Why Household Appliances Break Down — sai · Chỉ một khía cạnh
  • C
    The Dangers of Amateur Repairs — sai · Quan điểm nhà sản xuất, không phải trọng tâm
  • D
    France Leads Europe in Electronics Manufacturing — sai · Pháp chỉ là ví dụ

exercises.title: Câu 21–28 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 21–28).
exercises.passage:
1We tend to think of noise as a mere nuisance, an irritation that ends when the source falls silent. Medical researchers, however, have begun to treat it as a genuine public-health hazard. Chronic exposure to traffic and construction noise, they argue, elevates stress hormones, disrupts sleep and has been linked to cardiovascular disease.

2The difficulty lies in measurement. Whereas air pollution can be gauged by sensors at fixed locations, noise varies from street to street and from minute to minute. A study in Berlin attached portable recorders to volunteers for a month and discovered that those living near flight paths were exposed to peaks far above the levels recorded by official monitors, which are typically positioned away from buildings.

3Remedies exist, though they are seldom cheap. Quieter road surfaces can reduce traffic noise by several decibels, and triple glazing offers considerable protection indoors. Cities such as Paris have experimented with “noise radars” that photograph vehicles exceeding a limit, so that their owners can be fined.

4Some acousticians, nonetheless, caution against an exclusive focus on volume. They point out that a bubbling fountain and a jackhammer might register equally on a meter, yet only one is likely to unsettle passers-by. Designing cities that sound pleasant, they suggest, matters as much as designing cities that are merely quiet.

(Adapted from a public health magazine)
exercises.tr: Tiếng ồn là mối nguy sức khoẻ cộng đồng; khó đo vì thay đổi theo vị trí và thời gian; có giải pháp nhưng tốn kém; cần chú ý chất lượng âm thanh chứ không chỉ độ lớn.

items.q: In paragraph 1, the writer ____________.
opts: suggests that noise is more harmful than commonly assumed
argues that noise stops mattering once its source is silent
denies any link between noise and heart disease
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    suggests that noise is more harmful than commonly assumed — đúng · Tác giả nêu giới y khoa coi tiếng ồn là mối nguy y tế, vượt quan niệm “mere nuisance”.
  • B
    dismisses medical claims about noise — sai · Tác giả không bác bỏ mà trình bày
  • C
    argues that noise stops mattering once its source is silent — sai · Đó là quan niệm phổ biến mà tác giả phản bác
  • D
    denies any link between noise and heart disease — sai · Bài nói tiếng ồn liên quan bệnh tim mạch

items.q: The word “gauged” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ____________.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    compared — sai · compare = so sánh
  • B
    measured — đúng · gauge = đo lường ≈ measure.
  • C
    reduced — sai · reduce = giảm
  • D
    ignored — sai · ignore = phớt lờ

items.q: The word “those” in paragraph 2 refers to ____________.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    portable recorders — sai · recorders là thiết bị
  • B
    volunteers — đúng · “volunteers… those living near flight paths”.
  • C
    official monitors — sai · monitors ở câu sau
  • D
    flight paths — sai · flight paths là địa điểm

items.q: According to paragraph 2, why is noise difficult to measure?
opts: Levels vary greatly from place to place and moment to moment.
There are too many official monitors.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    Sensors cannot detect sound. — sai · Bài không nói thế
  • B
    Levels vary greatly from place to place and moment to moment. — đúng · “noise varies from street to street and from minute to minute”.
  • C
    Volunteers refuse to wear recorders. — sai · Bài không nhắc
  • D
    There are too many official monitors. — sai · Monitors lại đặt xa nhà

items.q: Which of the following best paraphrases the underlined sentence in paragraph 4?
opts: Creating a pleasing soundscape is as important as reducing volume.
Quiet cities are always more pleasant than noisy ones.
A merely quiet city is preferable to a pleasant-sounding one.
It is impossible to design a city that sounds pleasant.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    Creating a pleasing soundscape is as important as reducing volume. — đúng · “matters as much as” = quan trọng ngang nhau.
  • B
    Quiet cities are always more pleasant than noisy ones. — sai · “always” — quá tuyệt đối
  • C
    A merely quiet city is preferable to a pleasant-sounding one. — sai · ngược nghĩa (cho quiet quan trọng hơn)
  • D
    It is impossible to design a city that sounds pleasant. — sai · ngược nghĩa (không thể)

items.q: Which of the following would the writer NOT agree with?
opts: Noise can harm health in ways that go beyond annoyance.
Official monitors may underestimate the noise some people endure.
Reducing noise is generally an inexpensive undertaking.
Loudness alone does not determine how unsettling a sound is.
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    Noise can harm health in ways that go beyond annoyance. — sai · Tác giả đồng ý (đoạn 1)
  • B
    Official monitors may underestimate the noise some people endure. — sai · Tác giả đồng ý (đoạn 2)
  • C
    Reducing noise is generally an inexpensive undertaking. — đúng · Đoạn 3: “seldom cheap”.
  • D
    Loudness alone does not determine how unsettling a sound is. — sai · Tác giả đồng ý (đoạn 4)

items.q: In which paragraph does the writer mention a technological device used to enforce noise limits?
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    Paragraph 1 — sai · Đoạn 1 nói về hại sức khoẻ
  • B
    Paragraph 2 — sai · Đoạn 2 nói về đo lường
  • C
    Paragraph 3 — đúng · Đoạn 3: “noise radars” ở Paris.
  • D
    Paragraph 4 — sai · Đoạn 4 nói về chất lượng âm

items.q: In which paragraph does the writer compare two sounds of similar loudness?
items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: D
  • A
    Paragraph 1 — sai · Đoạn 1 không so sánh
  • B
    Paragraph 2 — sai · Đoạn 2 nói về đo
  • C
    Paragraph 3 — sai · Đoạn 3 nêu giải pháp
  • D
    Paragraph 4 — đúng · Đoạn 4: tiếng đài phun nước và máy khoan.

exercises.title: Câu 29–34 · Điền từ vào đoạn
exercises.instruction: Đọc đoạn văn rồi chọn phương án phù hợp nhất cho từng chỗ trống đánh số (câu 29–34).
exercises.passage:
JOIN OUR BEACH CLEAN-UP DAY!

Our coastline is under growing 29 from litter, and plastic waste in particular threatens marine life. On Saturday 14 June, volunteers of all ages will 30 at Sunrise Beach to give it a thorough clean. Here is how you can help:

• Collection: Gloves and bags will be 31 to every participant. Please sort the rubbish into recyclable and non-recyclable items so that it can be disposed of 32.

• Awareness: Our guides will explain how discarded fishing nets can 33 dolphins and turtles.

• Everyone is welcome, 34 you are experienced or not.

Together we can give our shoreline the care it deserves!

items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    threat — đúng · “under threat” là cụm cố định = bị đe doạ.
  • B
    danger — sai · “under danger” sai
  • C
    risk — sai · “under risk” sai (at risk)
  • D
    harm — sai · “under harm” sai

✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    assemble — đúng · “assemble at + place” = tập trung tại.
  • B
    attach — sai · attach/adopt/assess không hợp nghĩa
  • C
    adopt — sai
  • D
    assess — sai

✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    supplied — đúng · Bị động sau “will be”: “will be supplied to”.
  • B
    supplying — sai · V-ing/nguyên mẫu/danh từ đều sai sau will be
  • C
    supply — sai
  • D
    supplies — sai

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    responsible — sai · Tính từ/danh từ không bổ nghĩa cho động từ
  • B
    responsibly — đúng · Cần trạng từ bổ nghĩa cho “disposed of”: responsibly.
  • C
    responsibility — sai
  • D
    irresponsible — sai

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    involve — sai · involve = bao gồm
  • B
    entangle — đúng · “entangle” = làm vướng, hợp với lưới đánh cá.
  • C
    engage — sai · engage = thu hút
  • D
    embrace — sai · embrace = ôm

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    Although — sai · Although: không đi với or not
  • B
    Whether — đúng · “Whether … or not” = dù … hay không.
  • C
    Unless — sai · Unless: nếu không
  • D
    Despite — sai · Despite + N

exercises.title: Câu 35–40 · Điền từ vào đoạn
exercises.instruction: Đọc đoạn văn rồi chọn phương án phù hợp nhất cho từng chỗ trống đánh số (câu 35–40).
exercises.passage:
CODING FOR CHILDREN: SUMMER CAMP

Digital literacy is no longer optional; it is as 35 to children’s future as reading and arithmetic. Our two-week camp, led by experienced teachers, introduces young learners to programming through games and robotics.

• Beginners’ group: Pupils aged 8 to 10 will learn to 36 simple animations without any prior knowledge.

• Advanced group: Older participants, 37 have already mastered the basics, will design their own mobile applications.

• Teamwork: All activities are carried out in small groups, 38 encourages pupils to share ideas and solve problems collaboratively.

Places are 39, so parents are advised to reserve well in advance. Fees can be paid in 40 or in monthly instalments.

items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    essential — đúng · “as essential to” — tính từ.
  • B
    essentially — sai · trạng từ/danh từ sai vị trí
  • C
    essence — sai
  • D
    essentials — sai

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    bring in — sai · bring in = đưa vào
  • B
    put together — đúng · “put together” = lắp ráp, tạo ra.
  • C
    take over — sai · take over = tiếp quản
  • D
    set off — sai · set off = khởi hành

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    whom — sai · whom là tân ngữ
  • B
    who — đúng · Mệnh đề quan hệ chỉ người, làm chủ ngữ: who.
  • C
    whose — sai · whose + N
  • D
    which — sai · which chỉ vật

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    what — sai · what/that không dùng sau dấu phẩy
  • B
    which — đúng · “which” thay cho cả mệnh đề phía trước, sau dấu phẩy.
  • C
    that — sai · it gây lỗi nối câu
  • D
    it — sai

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    limit — sai · Các dạng khác sai từ loại
  • B
    limited — đúng · “Places are limited” — tính từ bị động.
  • C
    limiting — sai
  • D
    limitation — sai

✔ Đáp án đúng: B
  • A
    fully — sai · fully/fullness/fulfil sai cụm
  • B
    full — đúng · “in full” = trả đủ một lần.
  • C
    fullness — sai
  • D
    fulfil — sai

src: Đề tự soạn bám cấu trúc đề thi THPT 2026 (nâng cao B2–C2): AI & sáng tạo – kinh tế chú ý – quyền sửa chữa – tiếng ồn đô thị – dọn bãi biển – trại lập trình

title: Đề 11 · Đề tự soạn theo ma trận THPT 2026 (số 9) · Nâng cao

exercises.title: Câu 1–5 · Sắp xếp câu
exercises.instruction: Chọn phương án sắp xếp các câu/lời thoại thành một đoạn hội thoại hoặc đoạn văn hợp lý (câu 1–5).
exercises.passage:
Câu 1

a. Skyscraper farms, by contrast, stack crops vertically under artificial light, allowing harvests in the heart of the city.

b. Traditional agriculture requires vast tracts of land, which are increasingly scarce around expanding metropolises.

c. Critics, however, note that the electricity needed to power the lamps may cancel out the environmental benefits.

d. Their appeal lies in the shortened journey from field to table, which reduces both transport emissions and spoilage.

e. Unless renewable energy becomes cheaper, such projects will remain a niche rather than a mainstream solution.

Câu 2

a. Reader: Excuse me, how long can I keep these books?

b. Librarian: Three weeks, and you may renew them online if nobody has reserved them.

c. Reader: That’s helpful, thanks. I’ll probably need the extension.

Câu 3

Dear Sir or Madam,

a. Although the technician visited on 12 May, the fault persisted, and the machine has been unusable ever since.

b. I am writing to complain about the washing machine I purchased from your store on 2 May.

c. Within a week of delivery, the appliance began leaking water during its spin cycle.

d. I therefore request a full refund or, alternatively, a replacement of the same model.

e. I trust that you will resolve the matter promptly and look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully, Minh Chau

Câu 4

a. Doctor: What seems to be the trouble?

b. Patient: I’ve had a persistent cough for nearly three weeks, and it’s worse at night.

c. Doctor: Have you had a temperature or any difficulty breathing?

d. Patient: No temperature, but I do feel short of breath after climbing the stairs.

e. Doctor: I’d like to listen to your chest, and then we’ll arrange an X-ray.

Câu 5

a. This invention transformed the circulation of ideas almost overnight.

b. Before the fifteenth century, books were copied by hand, a process so laborious that only monasteries and the wealthy could afford them.

c. Within fifty years, millions of volumes had been printed across Europe, and literacy rates began to rise.

d. Then, around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg developed a movable-type press that allowed pages to be reproduced rapidly.

e. Consequently, authorities that had once monopolised knowledge found their influence steadily eroded.

items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    a – b – d – c – e — sai · a (by contrast) cần b làm đối chiếu trước
  • B
    b – d – a – c – e — sai · d (Their appeal) cần chủ ngữ đã nêu là vertical farms (a)
  • C
    b – a – d – c – e — đúng · b (đất khan hiếm) → a (by contrast: trang trại tầng cao) → d (Their appeal) → c (Critics, however) → e (Unless… niche).
  • D
    b – a – c – d – e — sai · c (Critics) phải sau mặt lợi d, rồi e kết luận
💡 “by contrast/however” đối lập với ý ngay trước.

✔ Đáp án đúng: C
  • A
    a – c – b — sai · c không thể đứng giữa a và b
  • B
    b – a – c — sai · b không mở đầu
  • C
    a – b – c — đúng · a hỏi thời hạn → b trả lời → c đáp lại.
  • D
    c – a – b — sai · c không mở đầu

✔ Đáp án đúng: D
  • A
    c – b – a – d – e — sai · c đứng trước b: chưa có mục đích thư
  • B
    b – a – c – d – e — sai · a (“the fault persisted”) cần c nêu lỗi trước
  • C

exercises.title: Câu 11–20 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 11–20).
exercises.passage:
1Few debates in the cultural sphere are as emotionally charged as the question of who should own the treasures of the past. For more than two centuries, the great museums of Europe and North America have displayed artefacts acquired during periods of colonial expansion, including bronzes, sculptures and funerary masks, often under circumstances that would today be regarded as ethically dubious. Source countries increasingly demand that these objects be returned, and some institutions have begun, hesitantly, to comply.

2Museums that resist restitution offer a range of defences. Their curators argue that universal collections allow visitors from every background to encounter humanity’s diverse achievements under a single roof, and that objects housed in well-funded institutions are better protected from theft, conflict and neglect. Some also point to legal obstacles: many founding charters prohibit the permanent disposal of items in their collections, and a change would require an act of parliament.

3Opponents of these arguments find them unconvincing. [I] The notion of safe-keeping, they contend, rings hollow when many objects were seized by force, and some were later damaged or lost in museum storage. [II] Moreover, several of the countries making claims have built modern museums designed to receive returned works. [III] In 2022, for instance, Germany began transferring hundreds of Benin Bronzes to Nigeria, a move widely regarded as a turning point. [IV] The legal objections, meanwhile, are increasingly viewed as problems of will rather than of law.

4Yet restitution is not without complications. Determining rightful ownership can be fiendishly difficult when borders have shifted, empires have collapsed and several communities claim the same object. Some scholars therefore favour long-term loans or shared custody, which, while stopping short of full return, would allow works to travel without settling every question of title. Critics of such compromises, however, regard them as a way of postponing the inevitable.

5Whatever the outcome of individual disputes, the debate has already altered the museum’s sense of purpose. Institutions that once saw themselves as neutral guardians of world heritage are now compelled to acknowledge the histories of their own collections, and to ask whose stories their galleries tell, and whose they omit.

(Adapted from a cultural heritage journal)
exercises.tr: Tranh luận về việc trả lại cổ vật cho nước gốc; các bảo tàng viện dẫn bảo quản và luật; phía phản đối bác bỏ, dẫn ví dụ Đức trả Benin Bronzes; khó xác định quyền sở hữu nên có giải pháp cho mượn dài hạn; cuộc tranh luận thay đổi vai trò bảo tàng.

exercises.passage:
1Platform-based work, from ride-hailing to freelance design, has been marketed as the liberation of the modern worker: no fixed hours, no overbearing manager and complete freedom to choose when to work. For many participants, however, the reality is considerably less glamorous. Earnings fluctuate unpredictably and, because workers are classified as independent contractors, they typically receive no sick pay, holiday pay or pension contributions.

2A survey of delivery couriers in six European cities revealed a striking pattern. Although most respondents valued flexibility, nearly half said they worked more hours than they would like, since each cancelled shift lowered their ranking in the algorithm that distributes jobs. Flexibility, in other words, was largely nominal.

3Defenders of the model counter that it provides a lifeline for students, parents and migrants who cannot easily secure conventional jobs. Regulating the sector too heavily, they warn, would drive platforms out of the market and leave the very people it seeks to protect without any income at all.

4Several governments are searching for a middle path. Spain now presumes that couriers are employees, while the United Kingdom has created a hybrid category with limited protections. It remains to be seen whether such compromises will hold, or whether platforms will simply find new ways to evade them.

(Adapted from a labour economics review)
exercises.tr: Gig economy được quảng cáo là tự do nhưng thu nhập bất ổn, thiếu phúc lợi; khảo sát shipper cho thấy tự do mang tính hình thức; phe ủng hộ cho rằng đó là cứu cánh; các chính phủ tìm giải pháp trung gian.

exercises.title: Câu 11–20 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 11–20).
exercises.passage:
1Since the discovery of penicillin in 1928, antibiotics have saved countless lives and turned once-fatal infections into minor inconveniences. Yet this triumph of modern medicine is now jeopardised by an unwelcome natural process: bacteria, subjected to repeated exposure, evolve defences that render the drugs ineffective. The World Health Organization warns that, unless the trend is reversed, routine operations such as hip replacements may again become dangerously risky.

2The fundamental cause is overuse. In many countries, antibiotics can be bought without a prescription, and patients frequently demand them for viral illnesses such as colds, against which they are powerless. Agriculture compounds the problem: in some regions, up to three-quarters of antibiotics are given to healthy livestock to promote growth, creating ideal conditions for resistant strains to flourish and spread to humans through food and water.

3Reversing the trend will not be easy. [I] Developing new antibiotics is expensive, and companies earn far more from medicines that patients take for life than from short courses of treatment. [II] As a result, few pharmaceutical firms have invested in the field, and the pipeline of promising drugs has nearly dried up. [III] Some governments have therefore proposed a “subscription” model, paying companies a fixed annual fee for access to new drugs regardless of how many are actually sold. [IV] Early trials in Britain suggest that the scheme could restore the commercial incentive without encouraging overuse.

4Individual behaviour matters, too. Health authorities urge patients to finish prescribed courses, never to share leftover pills and to accept that a doctor’s refusal to prescribe antibiotics for a cold is a sign of good practice, not negligence. Meanwhile, specialists stress that hospitals must adopt stricter hygiene, since resistant microbes spread most readily where vulnerable patients are concentrated.

5Ultimately, antibiotic resistance is a problem of collective action. Each unnecessary prescription may seem harmless in isolation, yet the cumulative effect is to erode a shared resource that no single country can replenish alone. Unless the incentives that govern doctors, farmers and manufacturers are realigned, the age of effective antibiotics may prove to have been a brief interlude in medical history.

(Adapted from a public health magazine)
exercises.tr: Vi khuẩn kháng kháng sinh do lạm dụng thuốc ở người và chăn nuôi; ít hãng phát triển thuốc mới vì lợi nhuận thấp; mô hình “đăng ký” được thử; cần cả hành vi cá nhân và bệnh viện; đây là bài toán hành động tập thể.

exercises.title: Câu 21–28 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 21–28).
exercises.passage:
1In an age of relentless advertising, the decision to own less has acquired the status of a lifestyle. Minimalists, as they are known, discard possessions that do not serve a clear purpose and resist the urge to replace them. Their philosophy is often misconstrued as asceticism, yet its proponents insist that the goal is not deprivation but clarity.

2Psychologists offer a plausible explanation for its appeal. Possessions, they note, demand attention: each object must be stored, cleaned, insured or repaired. A cluttered home can therefore generate a persistent, low-level stress that people scarcely notice until it disappears. Participants in one study who donated a third of their belongings reported feeling calmer within a month.

3Sceptics point out, however, that minimalism is a luxury available chiefly to those who can afford to replace discarded items if necessary. For families on tight budgets, keeping a spare coat or a rarely used tool is not clutter but insurance. Moreover, some critics argue that minimalism has itself become a consumer trend, with devotees purchasing expensive, sleek storage solutions in order to look uncluttered.

4Perhaps the most balanced view is that minimalism works best as a method rather than a creed. Asking whether an object genuinely adds value to one’s life is a useful habit, whether it leads to a nearly empty room or merely to a tidier cupboard.

(Adapted from a lifestyle magazine)
exercises.tr: Lối sống tối giản bị hiểu lầm là khổ hạnh nhưng nhằm sự rõ ràng; tâm lý học giải thích đồ đạc gây căng thẳng; người hoài nghi cho rằng đó là đặc quyền và đã thành xu hướng tiêu dùng; tối giản nên là phương pháp.

items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: A
  • A
    explains the aim of minimalism and corrects a common misunderstanding — đúng · “often misconstrued as asceticism… goal is not deprivation but clarity”.
  • B
    condemns people who own few possessions — sai · Tác giả không lên án
  • C
    claims that advertising has disappeared — sai · Bài nói quảng cáo “relentless”
  • D
    argues that minimalism requires extreme poverty — sai · Bài nói không phải khổ hạnh/nghèo

Cycling is a healthy and sustainable way to 35 around the city, but it is not entirely free of risk.

By following these simple guidelines, you will protect 40 and others.

Hue Festival Volunteer Programme

The Hue Festival is one of the biggest cultural events in Viet Nam. This year, we are looking 1 young volunteers to help visitors.

Last year, more than four hundred volunteers helped to welcome visitors from over thirty countries, and many of them described the experience as the highlight of their university years. The programme is coordinated by the city’s department of culture.

Duties

Volunteers will guide tourists, answer questions and 2 performers backstage. You must be able to speak basic English and 3 well in a team.

Benefits

Volunteers will receive a free uniform, meals and a certificate. It is a great chance to meet 4 people and learn about local traditions. Applications must be sent 5 30 November. 6 you have any questions, contact us at any time.

Selected volunteers will attend a two-day training course before the festival begins. Everyone who completes at least forty hours of service will receive an official certificate, which is highly regarded by employers and universities.

exercises.passage:
VOLUNTEERING

Volunteering means giving your time to help others without being paid. 7. It also helps volunteers to grow as people.

Numerous organisations rely entirely on volunteers. Fire services in remote areas, animal shelters and community kitchens would find it impossible to operate without the time and energy that ordinary people freely give.

Young people who volunteer often 8 and develop new skills. Some join groups that clean beaches, while others 9.

Employers like candidates with volunteering experience because it shows responsibility. Anyone 10 can start with a small activity. Even one hour a week 11.

Starting is easier than most people imagine. Schools, local councils and websites list opportunities for all ages and interests, so anyone who wants to help can find an activity that fits their schedule and talents.

(Adapted from a community website)

exercises.passage:
Learning with Artificial Intelligence

Artificial intelligence is changing education. AI programmes can 12 students’ answers and give instant feedback, which saves teachers a great deal of time.

Several schools have already tested these tools with encouraging results. In one pilot project, students who used an AI tutor for English grammar improved their test scores faster than those who studied only with textbooks.

Some applications adapt exercises to each learner’s level. Students who find a topic difficult receive 13 practice, while quick learners move on to harder tasks.

14, there are concerns. If students rely too 15 on AI, they may stop thinking for themselves. Teachers 16 that technology should support learning, not replace effort.

Nevertheless, educators remind us that machines cannot replace human relationships. A good teacher can sense when a student is worried or confused, and this kind of understanding remains an essential part of real learning.

17 used wisely, AI can make learning more personal and enjoyable.

exercises.title: Câu 23–32 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 23–32).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Climate change refers to long-term shifts in temperatures and weather patterns. [II] Natural factors have always influenced the climate, but since the nineteenth century human activities have been the main driver. [III] Burning coal, oil and gas for energy releases greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere. [IV]

2The effects are already visible. Glaciers are melting, sea levels are rising, and extreme weather such as floods and heat waves has become more frequent. Coastal cities and low-lying regions, including the Mekong Delta, are especially vulnerable.

3Responding to this challenge requires action at every level. Governments can set limits on emissions and invest in renewable energy. Businesses can enhance energy efficiency and reduce waste. Meanwhile, individuals can save electricity, use public transport and eat less meat.

4Some people argue that one person’s efforts are too small to matter. Nevertheless, when millions of people change their habits together, the combined effect can be considerable. Education is therefore essential to help citizens understand the issue.

(Adapted from a science website)
exercises.tr: Biến đổi khí hậu chủ yếu do con người đốt nhiên liệu hóa thạch; băng tan, nước biển dâng; chính phủ, doanh nghiệp, cá nhân cùng hành động; giáo dục rất quan trọng.

Where in paragraph 1 does the following sentence best fit?

items.xh:
✔ Đáp án đúng: D

  • B
    [II] — sai · vị trí trước đó chưa nêu nguyên nhân khí nhà kính nên "As a result" không có căn cứ.
  • C
    [III] — sai · vị trí trước đó chưa nêu nguyên nhân khí nhà kính nên "As a result" không có căn cứ.
  • D
    [IV] — đúng · "As a result" nối với việc khí nhà kính giữ nhiệt ([III]); đặt sau câu [III], tức vị trí [IV].

exercises.title: Câu 33–40 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 33–40).
exercises.passage:
1Every year, the Mid-Autumn Festival is celebrated across Viet Nam when the moon is at its roundest and brightest. Although it is frequently called the Children’s Festival, people of all ages take part in it.

2Traditionally, families prepare a tray of fruits and moon cakes to display and share. Children carry colourful lanterns, regularly shaped like stars or fish, and parade through the streets after dark. In numerous towns, lion dances attract enthusiastic crowds.

3The festival’s origins lie in the harvest season. Farmers, thankful for the year’s crops, would gather to enjoy the cooler weather and the full moon. Over time, legends about the moon, such as the story of Cuoi and the banyan tree, added a magical dimension.

4Today, the celebration has been influenced by modern life. Some people purchase ready-made moon cakes instead of baking them, and city children may receive plastic toys rather than handmade lanterns. Even so, the festival remains a time for family reunion.

(Adapted from a cultural guide)
exercises.tr: Tết Trung thu có mâm cỗ, đèn lồng, múa lân, nguồn gốc mùa thu hoạch và truyền thuyết; ngày nay có thay đổi nhưng vẫn là dịp đoàn viên.

exercises.title: Câu 1–6 · Điền từ vào đoạn
exercises.instruction: Đọc đoạn văn rồi chọn phương án phù hợp nhất cho từng chỗ trống đánh số (câu 1–6).
exercises.passage:
Sign Language

Sign language is a visual way of communicating that uses hand shapes, facial expressions and body movements. Millions of deaf people around the world 1 on it every day.

Deaf communities have their own rich cultures, including humour, poetry and storytelling that are performed entirely through signs. For many people, sign language is not just a means of communication but also a crucial part of who they are.

Many people think there is only one sign language, but this is not true. 2 country typically has its own version, and some have more than one. For 3, American Sign Language is quite different from British Sign Language.

Learning sign language can be rewarding. It helps hearing people 4 with deaf friends and understand their culture. More schools 5 it as an optional subject. 6 students who study it frequently report improved concentration.

In recent years, more universities have started to offer sign language courses, and some television programmes now include interpreters. These developments are helping to make society more inclusive for everyone.

(Adapted from an education magazine)

exercises.title: Câu 7–14 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 7–14).
exercises.passage:
1Studying in a group can be more productive than studying alone, provided that the group is well organised. Members can share notes, explain difficult ideas to each other and keep one another motivated.

2However, group study does not work for everyone. Some students get easily distracted by chatting, and a few members may leave the work to others. To avoid these challenges, experts recommend setting clear goals for each session, for example finishing a particular unit or solving ten exercises.

3Choosing the right partners is also important. Ideally, the group should include students with different strengths, so that each person can help the others. Four or five members is typically the best size; larger groups become hard to manage.

4Finally, groups should meet regularly in a quiet place and agree on simple rules, such as turning off phones. With these arrangements, group study can become an enjoyable and effective routine.

(Adapted from a study-skills guide)
exercises.tr: Học nhóm hiệu quả nếu có tổ chức: mục tiêu rõ, nhóm 4–5 người đa dạng, họp đều, có quy tắc.

Join Our Community Garden

Do you want to enjoy fresh vegetables 15 you grow yourself? Our community garden on Green Street is now open to everyone in the neighbourhood.

The garden was created on a piece of unused land that was once covered in rubbish. Thanks to the efforts of local residents, it now contains more than fifty plots, a small greenhouse and a shaded area where families can sit and share lunch.

What we offer

Each family can 16 a small plot of land for a low monthly fee. We provide tools, seeds and advice from 17 gardeners. No experience is needed.

Why join?

Gardening is a relaxing way to 18 outdoors and meet your neighbours. Children can learn where food comes from and 19 about the environment. Come and visit us 20 weekends.

Our next open morning will take place this Sunday from 8 a.m. to noon. Come along with your children, ask our experienced gardeners any questions you have, and discover how rewarding it is to grow your own food.

exercises.title: Câu 31–40 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Backpacking is a style of low-cost, independent travel in which people carry their belongings in a single bag. [II] Unlike package tours, it allows travellers to choose their own routes and stay as long as they like in each place. [III] Many young people see it as a way to learn about different cultures while experiencing freedom. [IV]

2One of the main attractions is the chance to meet people. Backpackers typically sleep in hostels, where they share rooms and kitchens with others from around the world. Friendships formed in this way often last for years, and travellers frequently exchange advice about the best places to visit, the cheapest transport and hidden gems off the tourist trail.

3Nevertheless, backpacking requires preparation. Travellers must research visa rules, keep their valuables safe and carry only essential items, since a heavy bag rapidly becomes a burden. Health insurance is also advisable in case of illness or accidents.

4Despite these challenges, many people consider backpacking a life-changing experience. It teaches independence, flexibility and problem-solving, which are useful long after the trip is over.

(Adapted from a travel magazine)
exercises.tr: Du lịch ba lô tự do, tiết kiệm, gặp gỡ bạn bè quốc tế; cần chuẩn bị visa, bảo hiểm, mang đồ gọn; mang lại sự độc lập và linh hoạt.

THE IMPORTANCE OF SLEEP

Sleep is not a luxury; it is a basic need. 1. During sleep, the body repairs itself and the brain organises memories.

Scientists are still discovering how important sleep is. During deep sleep, the body releases hormones that help children grow, and the immune system becomes stronger, which makes people less likely to catch common illnesses.

People who sleep too little 2 and make more mistakes at work or school. Over time, lack of sleep 3, such as heart disease.

To sleep better, try to 4 every day. Avoid screens an hour before bed, and 5.

Despite this, modern lifestyles frequently make good sleep difficult. Late-night screen time, irregular schedules and too much caffeine are among the main enemies of rest, and avoiding them is one of the simplest ways to enhance overall health.

(Adapted from a health magazine)

exercises.title: Câu 11–18 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 11–18).
exercises.passage:
1Online shopping has changed the way people purchase things. Instead of walking from shop to shop, consumers can browse thousands of products on a phone and have them delivered to their door within days.

2Convenience is the main reason for its success. Shops never close, and prices can be compared in seconds. Many websites also offer free delivery or discounts for first-time buyers. For people living in remote areas, online stores may be the only way to reach a wide variety of goods.

3On the other hand, there are drawbacks. Shoppers cannot examine products physically, so what arrives may look different from the photos. Returning items can be inconvenient, and personal data may be at risk if a website is not secure.

4Experts therefore advise buyers to read reviews, use secure payment methods and check the return policy. Used carefully, online shopping can save both time and money.

(Adapted from a consumer magazine)
exercises.tr: Mua sắm online tiện lợi, so sánh giá nhanh nhưng không xem được hàng, khó trả hàng, rủi ro dữ liệu; nên đọc đánh giá, thanh toán an toàn.

Are you looking for an exciting day out? The National Science Museum offers a wide 19 of interactive exhibits that both children and adults will enjoy.

The museum’s newest hall, which opened last month, is devoted to renewable energy. Visitors can generate electricity by pedalling a bicycle, test a model wind turbine and watch short films about the scientists who changed the world.

Exhibits

You can build a simple robot, 20 a flight simulator and explore the human body through a giant model. Special workshops are held 21 Saturday morning.

Visitor Information

The museum is open from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., 22 Mondays. Admission is free for children under six. 23 crowded weekends, we advise you to book tickets online. Large bags 24 in the cloakroom.

Guided tours are available in English and Vietnamese, and school groups can request special programmes for different age levels. Please note that the museum shop and café close thirty minutes before the exhibition halls.

exercises.passage:
Shopping Online

More and more people prefer to shop online. It saves time, offers lower prices and lets customers compare products 25 leaving home.

Online marketplaces have also given small businesses a chance to reach customers far beyond their local area. A family that makes handmade ceramics in a village can now sell its products to buyers in the capital or even abroad.

However, there are risks. Some sellers 26 fake goods, and customers cannot touch or try items before buying. It is advisable to purchase only from 27 websites with good reviews.

Delivery can also be a problem. Packages sometimes arrive late or 28. Consequently, always keep the receipt and 29 the item as soon as it arrives. 30 careful, shoppers can enjoy the benefits safely.

As the number of online shoppers continues to rise, authorities are introducing new rules to protect consumers. These include clearer return policies and penalties for websites that sell counterfeit goods.
