exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Over the last few decades, robots have become a common sight in factories around the world. [II] They are used to weld car parts, pack goods and move heavy loads. [III] Because robots do not tire, they can maintain the same quality of work through the night. [IV]

2The advantages for companies are clear: higher productivity, fewer errors and lower long-term costs. Robots can also take over tasks that are dangerous or unhealthy for people, such as working with toxic chemicals or in extreme heat. Numerous workers therefore welcome the change.

3However, automation also raises serious questions. When a robot replaces several workers, those workers must find new jobs, which is not always easy for older employees. Some economists predict that millions of jobs could disappear in the next twenty years.

4Others take a more optimistic view. They point out that new technology has always created new types of work, such as robot maintenance and programming. The key challenge, they argue, is to retrain workers rapidly enough to fill these new positions.

(Adapted from a business magazine)

exercises.passage:
1[I] Studying abroad has long been a dream for many young people. [II] It offers the opportunity to improve a foreign language, make international friends and gain a qualification that is recognised worldwide. [III] However, it is also a big step that requires careful thought. [IV]

2The first obstacle is cost. Tuition fees and living expenses can be several times higher than at home, so families must plan years in advance. Fortunately, many governments and universities offer scholarships, and some students work part-time to cover daily expenses.

3Another challenge is adapting to a new environment. Students may feel lonely, struggle with the climate or find the teaching style unfamiliar. Those who join clubs, talk to local students and keep in touch with family typically adjust more rapidly.

4Despite these difficulties, most graduates say the experience was worthwhile. It broadened their outlook and gave them confidence to tackle unfamiliar situations.

(Adapted from an education report)
exercises.tr: Du học mở rộng cơ hội ngôn ngữ, bạn bè, bằng cấp; khó khăn về chi phí và thích nghi; học bổng, câu lạc bộ giúp ích; cuối cùng đáng giá.

Exchange Student Programme

Are you interested in experiencing life in another country? Our exchange programme gives high school students the chance to 11 a year abroad.

Participants will be matched with host families who have been carefully selected and trained by our partner organisation. The aim is not only to learn a language but also to experience a different way of life from the inside.

Who can apply?

Students aged 16 to 18 12 have good grades and a strong interest in other cultures are welcome. You will live 13 a local host family and attend a local school.

How to apply

Applications must be 14 before 1 March. Successful candidates will be informed 15 email. Scholarships are available 16 students who need financial support.

Applicants will be asked to submit a short essay, two references and a recent school report. Interviews will be held in January, and successful candidates will be informed in February, in time to prepare for their departure.

a. Passenger: Does this bus go to the city centre?

b. Driver: Yes, but you need to change at Central Station.

c. Passenger: How much is the ticket?

d. Driver: It’s ten thousand dong.

a. Mr Tran: Excuse me, could I have a table for two?

a. I am writing to ask for permission to organise a charity book fair.

a. Public transport reduces traffic jams and air pollution.

b. Many big cities are investing in metro lines and electric buses.

c. It is also cheaper than owning a private car.

d. More people should therefore be encouraged to use it.

a. Many universities offer scholarships to talented students.

b. University fees can be a heavy burden for families.

c. Some cover the whole tuition, while others pay only part of it.

exercises.passage:
Coral Reefs in Danger

Coral reefs are frequently called the rainforests of the sea because they 22 a quarter of all marine species.

Reefs cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, yet they protect coastlines from storms and provide food and income for hundreds of millions of people. Their loss would therefore affect not only marine life but also human communities.

Unfortunately, rising sea temperatures cause corals to lose their colour, a process known 23 bleaching. Pollution and overfishing also damage reefs.

24 corals are slow-growing, they need decades to recover. Governments 25 marine parks where fishing is not allowed, and tourists are asked not to touch the coral.

Everyone can help by choosing sustainable seafood and 26 energy. 27 we act now, future generations may still see these beautiful ecosystems.

Scientists are testing new methods to help corals survive, such as growing heat-resistant varieties in laboratories and transplanting them onto damaged reefs. These efforts offer hope, but they cannot succeed unless global warming is slowed.

exercises.passage:
SCHOLARSHIPS

A scholarship is money awarded to students to help pay for their education. 28. Some are given for academic excellence, others for sports or artistic talent.

Competition for these awards can be intense, so it is crucial to prepare early. Students should keep a record of their achievements, ask teachers for reference letters and read the instructions of each programme very carefully.

To win a scholarship, you typically 29 and write a convincing essay. Interviews may also 30.

Many students do not apply because they think they will not qualify. 31. In fact, a clear plan and early preparation 32.

It is also worth looking beyond universities. Companies, charities and local governments often offer financial support to talented students, and many of these opportunities receive far fewer applications than the famous national awards.

(Adapted from an education website)

exercises.title: Câu 33–40 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 33–40).
exercises.passage:
1Public transport is one of the most effective ways to make cities greener. A single bus can carry as many passengers as forty cars, which means fewer vehicles on the road and less exhaust gas in the air.

2Cities that invest in good public transport also benefit economically. Workers reach their jobs more easily, and shops near stations attract more customers. In addition, commuters save money because they do not need to pay for parking or fuel.

3For public transport to succeed, however, it must be reliable and comfortable. Passengers will return to their cars if buses are late, crowded or dirty. Many cities have therefore introduced real-time information apps and dedicated bus lanes to improve the service.

4Lastly, people are more likely to use public transport when walking and cycling routes connect to stations. An integrated system, in which different modes of transport work together, offers the best results.

(Adapted from a transport journal)

exercises.passage:
Going Cashless

Cashless payment is becoming more popular. Numerous shoppers now pay 1 their phones instead of carrying notes and coins.

Supermarkets, taxis and even street vendors in countless cities now accept payments by scanning a code. For customers, this means no more searching for change, and for sellers it minimises the risk of handling substantial amounts of cash.

Mobile payment is fast and 2. It also helps shops to keep accurate records of sales. 3, there are some concerns about security. Users should never share their passwords, and they 4 always log out of public computers.

Elderly people may find the technology confusing, 5 banks offer training courses. 6 these challenges, experts expect cashless payment to keep growing.

Governments also encourage the shift because electronic transactions are easier to track, which helps to minimise tax evasion. Nevertheless, they remind people that some individuals, especially in rural areas, still depend on cash.

Câu 7

a. Customer: Is there a discount for students?

b. Cashier: Yes, you get ten per cent off with a valid card.

c. Customer: Here is my card.

d. Cashier: Thank you. That will be 180,000 dong.

Câu 8

a. Minh: What do you usually do at weekends?

b. Lan: I volunteer at the community library.

c. Minh: That sounds interesting. What do you do there?

d. Lan: I help children choose books and read to them.

Câu 9

Dear Neighbours,

a. We are organising a clean-up day in our street next Sunday.

b. We will start at 8 a.m. and finish around noon.

c. Gloves and bags will be provided.

d. We hope to see many of you there.

Best wishes, Hoa

Câu 10

a. Cities are usually several degrees hotter than the countryside.

b. This is known as the urban heat island effect.

c. Concrete and asphalt absorb heat during the day and release it at night.

d. Planting trees and building green roofs can help cool the city.

Câu 11

a. Many students listen to music while studying.

b. However, music with lyrics can distract the brain.

c. Calm instrumental music, by contrast, may improve concentration.

d. Students should therefore choose their study music carefully.

exercises.passage:
MUSIC AND THE BRAIN

Music is more than entertainment. 12. Scientists have found that listening to music activates several areas of the brain at once.

Brain scans demonstrate that when people listen to a song they love, a chemical associated with pleasure is released. This may explain why a favourite melody can instantly lift our spirits and even bring back vivid memories of the past.

Learning to play an instrument can 13 and enhance memory. Children who take music lessons often 14.

Music also affects our emotions. A cheerful song can 15, while slow melodies help us relax. For this reason, doctors sometimes 16.

Owing to these effects, music is now used in hospitals, schools and care homes. Patients who listen to calm music before surgery, for instance, often report feeling less anxious and need less medication.

(Adapted from a science website)

Music Festival for Teens

The Youth Music Festival will take place in Da Nang this July. Over thirty bands will 17 on three stages during the weekend.

Besides the main stage, there will be a small area for young musicians who have never performed in public. Anyone who wishes to take part can send a short recording, and the best three will be invited to play in front of a live audience.

Programme

Each day begins with workshops 18 by professional musicians. Visitors who are interested in 19 instruments can try them for free.

Tickets

A two-day ticket costs only 200,000 dong, 20 is a bargain. Tickets are 21 online until 30 June. Please arrive early 22 the gates may be crowded.

Food stalls, art displays and a clothes market will be open throughout the weekend. We encourage visitors to travel by public transport because parking near the venue is limited, and shuttle buses will run every fifteen minutes.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 23–30).
exercises.passage:
1Libraries have existed for thousands of years, yet they remain among the most valuable institutions in any community. A good library offers free access to books, newspapers, computers and quiet places to study.

2For students, the library is more than a collection of books. It provides reliable sources for research and a calm atmosphere that is hard to find at home. Numerous libraries also run reading clubs and workshops, where patrons can meet people with similar interests.

3In small towns and rural areas, libraries play an especially crucial role. Families who cannot afford countless books can borrow them at no cost, and children develop reading habits early. Some mobile libraries even travel by van or boat to reach remote villages.

4Today, numerous libraries are adapting to digital technology by lending e-books and offering free internet. Nevertheless, librarians emphasise that their main task remains the same: connecting people with knowledge.

(Adapted from a community magazine)
exercises.tr: Thư viện cung cấp sách, nơi học yên tĩnh, câu lạc bộ; quan trọng ở vùng nông thôn; thích nghi với sách điện tử.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Cities all over the world are getting hotter. [II] Buildings, roads and car parks made of concrete and asphalt absorb the sun’s heat and slowly release it, so temperatures stay high even at night. [III] This is known as the urban heat island effect. [IV]

2The consequences go beyond discomfort. Hot weather increases the use of air conditioners, which raises electricity demand and releases more greenhouse gases. It also threatens public health: elderly people and young children are particularly at risk of heat-related illnesses.

3Fortunately, there are ways to cool cities down. Planting trees provides shade and cools the air as water evaporates from leaves. Green roofs and light-coloured surfaces reflect sunlight instead of absorbing it. Some cities are also creating more parks and water features.

4Citizens can contribute by choosing public transport, switching off unused devices and supporting local tree-planting. Although each action seems small, together they can reduce the heat that cities produce.

(Adapted from an urban-planning report)
exercises.tr: Hiệu ứng đảo nhiệt đô thị do bê tông, nhựa đường; ảnh hưởng điện, sức khỏe; trồng cây, mái xanh, bề mặt sáng màu giúp giảm nhiệt.

  • C

  • D

exercises.title: Câu 6–13 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 6–13).
exercises.passage:
1Water covers about seventy per cent of the Earth, yet only a tiny fraction of it is fresh and available for human use. As the population grows, numerous regions face serious water shortages.

2Agriculture is the biggest consumer, using around seventy per cent of the world’s fresh water. Industry and households also play a part, with daily habits such as long showers and leaking taps wasting substantial amounts.

3Solutions exist at every level. Farmers can adopt drip irrigation, which delivers water directly to plant roots. Factories can recycle the water they use. At home, families can fix leaks, collect rainwater and choose efficient appliances.

4Governments have a role too. By setting fair prices and protecting rivers and lakes from pollution, they can encourage sensible use. Without such action, experts warn, water may become a cause of conflict between nations.

(Adapted from an environmental journal)
exercises.tr: Nước ngọt khan hiếm; nông nghiệp dùng nhiều nhất; tưới nhỏ giọt, tái chế, sửa rò rỉ; chính phủ bảo vệ nguồn nước.

exercises.passage:
Using Wearable Technology

Wearable devices such as smartwatches and fitness bands have 14 popular in recent years. They can count steps, monitor heart rate and even track sleep.

The market for these products is growing rapidly, and analysts expect sales to double within five years. Many people purchase them because they want to understand their bodies better and to set realistic goals for exercise and sleep.

Numerous users say that these devices 15 them to exercise more. Doctors also use the data to give 16 advice to patients.

Before choosing a device, consumers should compare features, battery life and price. It is also wise to read the privacy policy, so that you know exactly what happens to the information the device collects about you.

17, wearable technology is not perfect. Readings are sometimes inaccurate, and users may worry 18 the privacy of their data. 19 these problems, many people consider wearables a useful health tool.

MANAGING YOUR TIME

Time is the one resource that everyone has in equal amounts. 20. Students who plan their day typically achieve more with less stress.

Numerous students believe that they have no time to study, when in reality they waste it without noticing. Checking messages, moving between tasks and putting things off until the last minute can take away hours that could be spent more usefully.

A good plan should 21. For instance, difficult tasks are best done when you feel 22. It is also wise to include short breaks.

Many people lose hours to social media without realising it. Setting a timer can help you 23. With practice, good time management 24.

A simple technique is to divide work into short periods of focused study followed by a five-minute break. Over time, this method trains the brain to concentrate and makes even difficult subjects feel more manageable.

(Adapted from a study-skills guide)

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Traditional crafts, such as weaving, pottery and wood carving, are a crucial part of a nation’s cultural identity. [II] In Viet Nam, craft villages have passed down their skills from generation to generation for hundreds of years. [III] Many of these products are now sold in markets around the world. [IV]

2However, craft villages face serious challenges. Cheap factory-made goods compete with handmade ones, and many young people prefer to look for work in cities rather than learn the family trade. As a result, some skills are in danger of disappearing.

3Several initiatives aim to preserve these crafts. Some villages have opened workshops for tourists, who pay to try making a product themselves. Others use social media to reach customers abroad. Governments also support training programmes for young artisans.

4Nevertheless, long-term success depends on innovation. Craftspeople who combine traditional techniques with modern designs are more likely to attract new customers. In this way, heritage and economic development can go hand in hand.

(Adapted from a cultural report)
exercises.tr: Nghề thủ công là bản sắc văn hóa; bị hàng công nghiệp cạnh tranh, thiếu người trẻ; workshop du lịch, mạng xã hội, đào tạo và đổi mới giúp bảo tồn.

exercises.passage:
Language Learning Apps

Learning a foreign language has never been easier. Numerous apps 1 short daily lessons that fit into a busy schedule.

Research suggests that learners who study for only fifteen minutes a day frequently progress faster than those who cram once a week. Apps make this kind of regular practice easy because they send friendly reminders and track progress over time.

Most apps use games to keep users motivated. You earn points, 2 levels and compete with friends. Some even recognise your voice and correct your pronunciation 3 real time.

However, apps cannot replace real conversation. Learners should 4 speaking with native speakers whenever possible. 5 they use an app regularly, their vocabulary will grow steadily. 6, progress needs patience.

Of course, the best application is the one that you will actually use. Many offer a free trial, so it is worth testing a few before you decide, and you should choose the one that matches your level and learning style.

Charity Fun Run

The annual Fun Run will take place in the city park on Sunday morning. All the money raised 7 be donated to children in need.

Registration opens at 7 a.m. at the main gate, and every participant will be given a numbered vest and a map of the route. Medical staff and first-aid stations will be available along the way in case of emergency.

Participants 8 choose between a 3-kilometre and a 5-kilometre route. Water stations will be located 9 the route.

Everyone who finishes will receive a medal and a T-shirt. 10 you cannot run, you can still volunteer. We are 11 for helpers to hand out water. 12 up today!

Last year, the event raised more than two hundred million dong, which was used to build a library for a primary school in a mountain village. This year, we hope to double that amount with the support of runners like you.

exercises.passage:
Câu 13

a. Customer: Two tickets for the seven o’clock film, please.

b. Clerk: Which film would you like to see?

c. Customer: The new science fiction movie.

d. Clerk: That will be 180,000 dong.

Câu 14

a. Mai: Did you enjoy the film?

b. Tom: Very much. The special effects were amazing.

c. Mai: I agree, but the story was a bit slow.

d. Tom: Maybe, but I liked the ending.

Câu 15

Dear Editor,

a. I am writing about the article on school uniforms in your last issue.

b. I strongly disagree with the author’s opinion.

c. Uniforms make students equal and help them focus on study.

d. I hope you will publish my letter.

Yours faithfully, Quang

Câu 16

a. In cities, space for gardens is limited.

b. Vertical farming grows plants in layers inside buildings.

c. It uses much less land and water than traditional farming.

d. As a result, fresh vegetables can be produced close to consumers.

Câu 17

a. Running is a simple and inexpensive way to stay fit.

b. It needs no equipment except a good pair of shoes.

c. Regular runners usually sleep better and feel less stressed.

d. Beginners should start slowly and increase distance gradually.

exercises.title: Câu 18–27 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 18–27).
exercises.passage:
1[I] The cinema has been a popular form of entertainment for over a century. [II] Early films were silent and in black and white, yet audiences were amazed to see moving pictures on a screen. [III] Sound arrived in the late 1920s, followed by colour a few years later. [IV]

2Today, film-making is a complex industry that involves hundreds of specialists, from directors and actors to sound engineers and visual-effects artists. A single blockbuster can cost more than a hundred million dollars and take several years to complete.

3Streaming services have changed how people watch films. Viewers can now enjoy new releases at home, on their phones or tablets. Some critics worry that this trend will empty cinemas, but others believe that the shared experience of a big screen can never be replaced.

4Film festivals play a crucial role by promoting independent and foreign films that might otherwise go unnoticed. They give young directors a chance to show their work to international audiences.

(Adapted from a media guide)
exercises.tr: Điện ảnh phát triển từ phim câm đến công nghiệp lớn; streaming thay đổi cách xem; liên hoan phim giúp đạo diễn trẻ.

VERTICAL FARMING

Vertical farming is a new method of growing crops. 28. Instead of wide fields, plants are stacked in tall indoor structures.

The idea was first proposed by a professor of public health, who calculated that a thirty-storey building could produce enough food for ten thousand people. At first, numerous experts doubted that the plan was realistic.

This approach uses LED lights and recycled water, so it can 29. Farms can be built inside warehouses in the heart of a city, which means food 30.

Critics point out that the electricity costs are high. 31. Supporters reply that prices 32 as technology enhances.

Today, vertical farms operate in cities such as Singapore, Tokyo and New York. They supply supermarkets and restaurants with fresh herbs and salad leaves, and engineers are working to grow staple crops such as rice in the same way.

(Adapted from an agricultural journal)

exercises.title: Câu 33–40 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 33–40).
exercises.passage:
1Learning a language is a long journey, and numerous beginners give up too soon. Experts say that the secret is not talent but consistency: practising a little every day is more effective than studying for hours once a week.

2One useful method is to surround yourself with the language. You can change your phone settings, listen to songs and watch films with subtitles. In this way, you meet new words in authentic contexts and remember them more easily.

3Making mistakes is also part of the process. Learners who are afraid of errors frequently stay silent, while those who speak freely improve faster. Teachers therefore encourage students to see mistakes as opportunities to learn.

4Finally, setting small goals keeps motivation high. Learning five new words a day, For instance, is realistic and gives a sense of achievement.

(Adapted from a language-teaching blog)
exercises.tr: Học ngoại ngữ cần kiên trì mỗi ngày, tạo môi trường ngôn ngữ, coi lỗi là cơ hội, đặt mục tiêu nhỏ.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 1–8).
exercises.passage:
1Friendship plays a vital role in our well-being. Research suggests that people with close friends are happier, healthier and even live longer than those who feel isolated.

2Good friendships are built on trust and mutual respect. Friends celebrate each other’s successes and offer support when times are hard. They also feel comfortable being honest, which helps them to grow as individuals.

3Technology has changed how friends communicate. Messaging apps make it straightforward to stay in touch across great distances. Nevertheless, experts warn that online contact cannot completely replace meeting face to face, where body language and tone of voice add meaning.

4Maintaining friendships requires effort. Making time to talk, remembering crucial dates and apologising after a quarrel are all small gestures that keep bonds strong.

(Adapted from a psychology magazine)
exercises.tr: Tình bạn tốt cho sức khỏe; dựa trên tin cậy, tôn trọng; công nghệ giúp nhưng không thay gặp mặt; cần duy trì.

DRONES IN EVERYDAY LIFE

Drones were once used only by the military. 9. Today, they are common in photography, farming and delivery services.

Small drones can now carry cameras that produce images of astonishing quality, allowing film-makers to capture scenes that were once impossible without a helicopter. Farmers also use them to check the health of crops over large areas in minutes.

Rescue teams use drones to 10 in areas that are challenging to reach. Some companies 11 to deliver small packages within minutes.

However, drones raise privacy concerns. Numerous countries 12 about where they can fly. Experts believe that clear laws 13.

As the technology develops, new uses will appear that we cannot yet imagine. The challenge for society is to benefit from these possibilities while ensuring that drones are used safely and respectfully.

(Adapted from a technology magazine)

Eco-Lodge in Cat Ba

Experience nature at its best at our eco-lodge on Cat Ba Island. All rooms are built 14 local wood and powered by solar energy.

The lodge is surrounded by tropical forest and overlooks a quiet bay where visitors can watch monkeys play at sunrise. All food is prepared from local ingredients, and wastewater is treated and reused for the gardens.

Guests can join kayaking trips, bird-watching tours and cooking classes 15 local ingredients. Each tour is led by a guide 16 knows the island well.

We encourage guests 17 plastic bottles and to save water. 18 your stay, we will plant a tree in your name. Book now 19 a 10% early discount.

Guests who stay for three nights or more will receive a free guided hike. We also welcome families with children, and our staff can arrange activities such as fishing and bird-watching to suit all ages.

exercises.passage:
Câu 20

a. Tom: Would you like to try my homemade cake?

b. Anna: Thank you. It looks delicious.

c. Tom: I hope you like it. It’s my grandmother’s recipe.

d. Anna: It’s wonderful. Could you share the recipe?

Câu 21

a. Doctor: What seems to be the problem?

b. Patient: I’ve had a sore throat for three days.

c. Doctor: Let me have a look. Open your mouth, please.

d. Patient: Is it serious?

Câu 22

Dear Linh,

a. Thank you for inviting me to your birthday party.

b. I would love to come, but I have a family dinner that evening.

c. I hope you have a wonderful time.

d. Let’s meet up next week to celebrate.

Love, Mai

Câu 23

a. True friends support you in both good and difficult times.

b. Friendship is one of the most valuable things in life.

c. They listen without judging and tell you the truth kindly.

d. It is therefore worth spending time to keep these relationships strong.

Câu 24

a. These small aircraft can fly over fields and collect detailed images.

b. Drones are now widely used in agriculture.

c. Farmers analyse the images to find out which areas need water.

d. This saves both time and resources.

exercises.passage:
Healthy Snacks

Numerous students feel hungry between meals and 25 for sweets or chips. These snacks are tasty but contain a lot of sugar and salt.

Nutritionists explain that the secret is to choose snacks that contain protein and fibre, because they keep you full for longer. A handful of almonds, For instance, is a far better choice than a packet of biscuits.

Healthier choices include fresh fruit, nuts and yoghurt. They give you energy 26 making you feel heavy. 27 you prepare snacks at home, you can control what goes into them.

Schools 28 promote healthy eating by changing canteen menus. 29, students should drink water instead of fizzy drinks. 30 habits like these, we can safeguard our health.

Reading food labels is another useful habit. Countless products described as ‘healthy’ contain surprising amounts of added sugar, so it is wise to check the list of ingredients before you purchase.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Street food is an essential part of Vietnamese culture. [II] From a bowl of pho in the morning to grilled pork noodles at lunch, vendors serve tasty meals at very low prices. [III] Many tourists say that trying street food is the highlight of their trip. [IV]

2Part of its charm lies in the atmosphere. Customers sit on small plastic stools beside the road, watching the cook prepare each dish in front of them. Recipes are often handed down through families, with each vendor adding a personal touch.

3Yet street food faces challenges. Rapid urbanisation means that vendors are sometimes moved from busy streets, and concerns about hygiene have led authorities to introduce stricter rules. Some vendors worry that these regulations will raise their costs.

4Many people suggest a balanced approach: improving food safety through training and clean water supply while preserving the lively character of street markets. With such measures, this beloved tradition can continue to thrive.

(Adapted from a travel guide)

E-SPORTS

Electronic sports, or e-sports, are organised video-game competitions. 1. Teams from different countries compete for large prizes.

The industry has grown rapidly over the past decade. Some tournaments now offer prize money that exceeds that of traditional sports, and the best players are treated like celebrities by their fans around the world.

Supporters say that e-sports 2 and quick decision-making. Players must also 3 in order to win.

Critics, however, worry that young people may spend too many hours in front of screens. 4. Parents 5 time limits and encourage other activities.

Whether e-sports will become part of major events such as the Olympic Games is still being debated. What is certain is that the number of young people who follow and play them is unlikely to fall.

(Adapted from a gaming magazine)

Public Speaking Course

Many people feel nervous when they speak 6 public. Our course will help you build confidence and deliver clear, interesting presentations.

Our trainers are professional speakers and university lecturers who understand that fear of speaking is very common. In a supportive atmosphere, you will learn how to turn nervous energy into enthusiasm and keep your audience interested.

Course content

You will learn how to organise your ideas, use your voice effectively and 7 eye contact with the audience. Each participant will practise 8 short speeches in a friendly group.

Details

The course 9 eight weeks. Classes are held on Tuesday evenings. The fee is 1.5 million dong, 10 includes all materials. Places are 11, so register now.

At the end of the course, each participant will give a ten-minute presentation to an invited audience and receive a certificate. Past students report that they now feel more confident in job interviews and in class.

exercises.instruction: Đọc đoạn văn rồi chọn phương án phù hợp nhất cho từng chỗ trống đánh số (câu 12–17).
exercises.passage:
Mangrove Forests

Mangrove forests grow along tropical coasts, where fresh water meets salt water. Their roots protect the shore 12 strong waves and storms.

Despite their importance, mangroves have disappeared at an alarming rate. Over the past fifty years, nearly a third of the world’s mangrove forests have been cleared for shrimp farms, ports and tourist resorts.

These forests are also home to numerous species of fish, crabs and birds. Local people depend 13 them for food and income. 14, large areas have been cleared to make way for shrimp farms.

Without mangroves, coastal villages 15 more flooding. Fortunately, countless communities are planting new trees, and some companies 16 them by funding projects. 17 more people become aware, these forests will be saved.

Local communities are now leading restoration projects, planting thousands of seedlings along the coast. Early results are encouraging, and scientists believe that healthy mangroves can protect villages from storms for generations.

exercises.title: Câu 23–32 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 23–32).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Mangrove forests are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth. [II] They grow in muddy coastal areas where few other trees can survive. [III] Their tangled roots slow down waves and trap sediment, which protects the coastline from erosion. [IV]

2Mangroves also store large amounts of carbon, in some cases more than tropical rainforests. When they are cleared, this carbon is released into the atmosphere, which contributes to global warming. In addition, mangroves serve as nurseries for young fish, so their loss minimises fish populations and the incomes of local fishing communities.

3Despite their value, around a third of the world’s mangroves have disappeared over the last fifty years, mainly owing to shrimp farming and urban development. Conservation groups are now working with villagers to restore damaged areas by planting seedlings.

4Restoration is not easy, however. Seedlings must be planted in the right places and protected from strong waves until they are established. Success therefore depends on careful planning and the long-term involvement of local people.

(Adapted from an ecology report)
exercises.tr: Rừng ngập mặn bảo vệ bờ biển, lưu trữ carbon, nơi sinh sản của cá; bị mất do nuôi tôm; cần phục hồi cẩn thận.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 33–40).
exercises.passage:
1Museums are frequently seen as quiet places for looking at old objects, but many have transformed into lively learning centres. Interactive displays allow visitors to touch, listen and even take part in activities that bring history to life.

2For students, a museum visit can be far more memorable than reading a textbook. Seeing a real artefact, such as an ancient tool or a soldier’s letter, creates an emotional connection with the past. Guides also help visitors to interpret what they see.

3Technology is playing a growing role. Some museums offer virtual tours, so people can explore their collections from home. Others use augmented reality to show how an ancient city might have looked.

4Despite these innovations, museums face financial pressure. Many depend on government funding and ticket sales, which have fallen in recent years. They therefore seek new partners and donors to keep their doors open.

(Adapted from a culture magazine)
exercises.tr: Bảo tàng trở thành trung tâm học tập sống động, dùng công nghệ ảo, nhưng thiếu kinh phí.

exercises.passage:
Electric Vehicles

Electric vehicles are becoming more common on our roads. Unlike petrol cars, they produce 1 exhaust gas, which makes the air cleaner.

The number of electric cars sold worldwide has risen sharply in the past five years, helped by government incentives and better batteries. Some countries have even announced plans to ban the sale of new petrol vehicles within the next two decades.

Charging an electric car costs 2 than buying petrol, and the engines need less maintenance. 3, the high purchase price remains an obstacle for numerous families.

Another problem is the shortage of charging stations. Governments 4 build more of them. 5 the number of stations increases, more people will switch. 6 cities will enjoy quieter streets and cleaner air.

Still, experts remind us that electric cars are only part of the solution. Cities also need good public transport, safe cycling routes and cleaner sources of electricity to make a real difference to the environment.

PREVENTING BULLYING

Bullying is a severe problem in numerous schools. 7. It can take the form of insults, rumours or online messages.

Bullying has grave consequences for everyone involved. Victims may lose confidence, avoid school and suffer from long-term anxiety, while those who bully others are more likely to face problems with the law later in life.

Victims 8 and may find it hard to concentrate. They may also 9 because they feel ashamed.

Schools can minimise bullying by 10. Students who witness an incident should 11.

Experts agree that early action is essential. Teachers should respond rapidly to complaints, parents should talk openly with their children, and students should be encouraged to stand up for classmates who are treated unfairly.

(Adapted from a school counselling guide)

exercises.title: Câu 17–24 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 17–24).
exercises.passage:
1Eating locally produced food has become a popular trend. Shoppers visit farmers’ markets or choose products labelled with their place of origin, believing that they are fresher and healthier.

2There are several advantages. Because local food does not travel far, it needs less packaging and fuel, which reduces pollution. Buying it also keeps money within the community, supporting small farmers who might otherwise struggle to compete with substantial companies.

3Nevertheless, local food is not always the best choice. Some products cannot be grown in certain climates, and out-of-season produce may require heated greenhouses that use more energy than transport does. It is therefore crucial to consider each product individually.

4Consumers who want to make a difference can start simply: learn which fruit and vegetables are in season, ask where the food comes from and avoid waste.

(Adapted from a food magazine)
exercises.tr: Thực phẩm địa phương ít đóng gói, hỗ trợ nông dân nhưng không phải lúc nào cũng tốt nhất; nên cân nhắc.

exercises.title: Câu 31–40 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Many young people feel overwhelmed when they finish high school and have to decide what to do next. [II] Some choose to take a “gap year”, a period of time between school and university or work. [III] During this time, they may travel, volunteer or take temporary jobs to gain experience. [IV]

2Supporters of the idea argue that a gap year helps students to mature. Away from the classroom, they learn to manage money, solve practical problems and adapt to unfamiliar environments. Many return with a clearer idea of the career they wish to pursue.

3Critics, however, worry that students may lose their study habits or find it hard to return to education. A gap year can also be expensive, especially if it involves travelling abroad, so not every family can afford it.

4To get the most from a gap year, experts recommend making a plan with clear goals, such as learning a language or completing a volunteer project. Without such a plan, the year may pass without any real benefit.

(Adapted from a career-guidance website)
exercises.tr: Năm nghỉ sau phổ thông giúp trưởng thành nhưng tốn kém và cần kế hoạch.

exercises.instruction: Đọc đoạn văn rồi chọn phương án phù hợp nhất cho từng chỗ trống đánh số (câu 6–11).
exercises.passage:
Sustainable Fashion

Fast fashion means producing cheap clothes rapidly to follow the latest trends. Consumers buy more clothes than ever, 6 many of them are worn only a few times.

Some of the world’s best-known brands are now taking steps to enhance. They are using recycled fibres, reducing water consumption and publishing information about the factories where their clothes are made.

This habit creates enormous waste. The fashion industry is responsible 7 about ten per cent of global carbon emissions and uses vast amounts of water.

Sustainable fashion offers an alternative. It encourages people to buy fewer, better-quality items and to 8 old clothes instead of throwing them away. 9, second-hand shops are growing fast.

You can also 10 clothes with friends or repair them. 11 these small steps, we can minimise the industry’s impact.

However, real change depends on consumers as well. By asking questions about where and how our clothes are produced, and by buying only what we need, we can encourage the whole industry to become more responsible.

First Aid Course

Accidents can happen anywhere, and knowing first aid can 12 lives. Our one-day course is open to everyone aged sixteen or older.

The training will be delivered by qualified instructors from the Red Cross, who will use real equipment and realistic scenarios to make the lessons memorable. Participants will practise each skill several times until they feel confident.

Topics

You will learn how to treat cuts and burns, help someone who is choking and 13 CPR. Trainers are experienced nurses 14 patiently answer all questions.

Information

The course takes place 15 the Red Cross building. Participants will receive a certificate 16 completion. 17 places are limited, early booking is recommended.

Anyone who completes the course will receive a certificate that is valid for two years. Please wear comfortable clothing, as you will be kneeling on the floor, and bring a bottle of water and a notebook.

exercises.passage:
1Natural disasters such as earthquakes, floods and typhoons cause great damage every year. Although they cannot be prevented, their effects can be reduced through preparation.

2Early-warning systems are among the most effective tools. For instance, satellites can track a typhoon for days, giving communities time to evacuate. In earthquake zones, buildings constructed with flexible materials are much less likely to collapse.

3Education also saves lives. Schools in disaster-prone areas teach children what to do during an emergency, and families prepare emergency kits containing water, food, a torch and basic medicines.

4After a disaster, rebuilding takes time. International aid and volunteer help are frequently essential, but experts stress that local people should take part in planning so that the new homes meet their real needs.

(Adapted from a geography textbook)

exercises.passage:
1[I] Fashion trends change faster than ever before. [II] Fast-fashion brands release new collections every few weeks, encouraging shoppers to buy more and discard clothes rapidly. [III] As a result, millions of tonnes of textiles end up in landfills every year. [IV]

2The environmental cost is enormous. Producing a single cotton shirt can require thousands of litres of water, and synthetic fabrics release microplastics when washed. Furthermore, dyeing and finishing processes often pollute rivers near factories, harming local communities.

3Some brands are now responding by using recycled materials and offering repair services. Consumers are also changing: second-hand shopping and clothes-swapping events are growing in popularity, especially among young people who care about the environment.

4Ultimately, the most sustainable garment is the one that already exists. By buying less, choosing durable items and wearing them for longer, shoppers can significantly reduce fashion’s footprint.

(Adapted from a sustainability report)

Wildlife Rescue Centre

Our rescue centre cares for animals that have been injured or 1 by their owners. Every year, we help over two thousand creatures return to the wild.

The centre treats more than fifty types of animals, from small birds to large monkeys. Veterinarians work alongside volunteers to provide medical care, and each animal is released only when experts are sure that it can survive in its natural habitat.

How you can help

You can donate money, adopt an animal or become a volunteer. Volunteers feed the animals, clean their cages and 2 visitors around the centre.

Opening hours

The centre is open 3 Tuesday to Sunday, 4 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Admission is free, but donations are 5 welcome. Please do not feed the animals, 6 it may harm them.

Educational visits for schools are available on weekday mornings. Students can learn about the dangers of the wildlife trade and see how they can help to safeguard animals in their own neighbourhoods.

exercises.passage:
1Many people spend hours every day on social media without thinking about the safety of their personal information. Yet every photo, location tag and birthday post can give strangers clues about who you are and where you live.

2Criminals use this information to steal identities or to trick people into revealing passwords. One common method is “phishing”, in which a fake message appears to come from a bank or a friend and asks the receiver to click a suspicious link.

3To stay safe, experts recommend checking privacy settings regularly and accepting friend requests only from people you know. Two-step verification, which sends a code to your phone, adds another layer of protection.

4Finally, think before you post. Once something is online, it can be copied and shared, even if you delete it later. Treat your digital footprint as carefully as your real-life reputation.

(Adapted from a cyber-security website)
exercises.tr: Thông tin cá nhân trên mạng dễ bị lợi dụng (lừa đảo phishing); kiểm tra quyền riêng tư, xác thực hai bước, cân nhắc trước khi đăng.

Parents can support these efforts by asking about the school’s menu and by providing healthy breakfasts at home. When families and schools cooperate, children are far more likely to develop good eating habits for life.

Staying Safe Online

The internet offers great opportunities for learning and entertainment, but it also has risks. Many young people share personal information 20 realising how it might be used.

Teenagers are frequently more confident online than they are in real life, which can lead them to take risks they would never take face to face. A friendly stranger in a chat room may not be who he or she claims to be.

To safeguard yourself, create strong passwords that contain letters, numbers and symbols. Never share them 21 anyone. Be careful about clicking links in messages from people 22 you do not know.

If you are treated badly online, do not reply. 23, save the evidence and tell a trusted adult. 24 the website offers a reporting tool, use it. 25 these rules, you can enjoy the internet safely.

Parents and teachers should talk openly about these dangers, rather than simply banning devices. Young people who understand the reasons behind the rules are much more likely to follow them and to ask for help when a problem occurs.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Lantern festivals are celebrated in many Asian countries, but each place gives them its own character. [II] In Hoi An, the old town switches off its electric lights on the night of the full moon every month. [III] Thousands of silk lanterns of different colours then glow along the streets and the river. [IV]

2Lantern making is a skilful craft. Artisans bend bamboo into frames, stretch silk or paper over them and paint delicate patterns by hand. A good lantern can take several hours to complete, which explains why visitors are eager to purchase one as a souvenir.

3The festival also brings economic benefits. Hotels, restaurants and shops are fully booked, and local boat owners earn extra income by carrying tourists along the river to release floating lanterns.

4However, substantial crowds can cause problems such as rubbish and noise. Local authorities have therefore begun limiting the number of floating lanterns and encouraging visitors to use biodegradable materials. These measures aim to protect the old town’s peaceful atmosphere.

(Adapted from a cultural tourism guide)
exercises.tr: Lễ hội đèn lồng Hội An đẹp, nghề thủ công, lợi ích kinh tế nhưng cần kiểm soát rác và tiếng ồn.

exercises.passage:
1[I] Every year, around eight million tonnes of plastic enter the world’s oceans. [II] Bottles, bags and fishing nets drift across the water, harming marine life along the way. [III] Turtles, For instance, frequently mistake floating bags for jellyfish and swallow them. [IV]

2Cleaning up this waste is a huge challenge. Specially designed boats and floating barriers can collect large pieces from the surface, but small fragments are almost impossible to remove. Scientists estimate that cleaning the oceans entirely would take decades, even with the best technology.

3For this reason, many experts argue that the priority should be to stop plastic from reaching the sea in the first place. Rivers carry much of the waste from cities, so installing barriers in rivers and improving waste collection in coastal towns are cost-effective solutions.

4Consumers also play a part. Choosing reusable bags and bottles minimises demand for single-use plastic. When prevention and cleaning are combined, the oceans have a real chance to recover.

(Adapted from an environmental news site)
exercises.tr: Nhựa đại dương gây hại sinh vật, khó dọn hết; cần ngăn từ nguồn và dọn dẹp, người tiêu dùng góp sức.

Beach Clean-up Day

Join us this Saturday for a beach clean-up at My Khe Beach! Everyone is welcome to 16 and help keep our coastline beautiful.

Last year, more than three hundred volunteers collected over two tonnes of rubbish in just four hours. Much of it was plastic, including bottles, bags and fishing nets that can harm marine animals and spoil the beauty of the beach.

What to bring

Please bring a hat, sunscreen and a bottle of water. Gloves and rubbish bags 17 by the organisers. Wear comfortable clothes 18 can get dirty.

Schedule

We will gather at 6 a.m. and work 19 nine o’clock. Breakfast will be served afterwards. 20 you can only stay for an hour, your help is still valuable. 21 you for caring about our planet!

Everyone who joins will receive a free T-shirt and a certificate of participation. Schools and companies are encouraged to bring teams, and the group that collects the most rubbish will win a special prize.

exercises.passage:
LEARNING AT A DISTANCE

Distance learning allows students to attend classes without going to school. 22. It became especially widespread when schools had to close.

The flexibility of this method attracts numerous learners, especially those who live far from schools or have jobs and family responsibilities. They can choose the time and place of study, and they can repeat lessons as many times as necessary.

Students can 23 and revisit recorded lessons whenever they like. Teachers 24 video calls and online platforms to explain new topics.

However, learners must be self-disciplined. Those who lack motivation 25. Schools 26 by giving clear schedules and regular feedback.

Teachers, too, have had to adapt. They need to design lessons that keep students interested on screen, and they must find ways to check understanding without seeing learners’ faces in a classroom.

(Adapted from an education report)

exercises.passage:
Reading Habits

Reading is one of the best habits a student can develop. It expands vocabulary, enhances imagination and 27 the mind sharp.

Many successful people say that reading has shaped their lives. Libraries, bookshops and online platforms now offer millions of titles, so it has never been easier to find a book that matches your interests and your level.

Unfortunately, numerous teenagers read 28 than before because they spend so much time on screens. To build a reading habit, start with books that match your interests. 29 you set aside twenty minutes every day, you will soon finish several books.

Joining a book club also helps, 30 you can discuss stories with others. Libraries and bookshops frequently organise events 31 readers meet authors. 32 reading regularly, you will become a better writer too.

Keeping a simple reading diary can also be motivating. Writing a few lines about each book helps you remember what you have learned and gives a satisfying record of your progress over the months.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 33–40).
exercises.passage:
1Reading is frequently described as a window to other worlds, and its benefits go far beyond entertainment. Studies demonstrate that people who read regularly have larger vocabularies and better writing skills.

2Reading fiction in particular helps readers understand other people’s feelings. By following characters through difficult situations, they develop empathy, which improves relationships in real life. Non-fiction, meanwhile, provides information that can broaden one’s knowledge.

3Despite these advantages, reading rates among young people are falling. Many say they lack time or find books less exciting than videos. Schools can respond by letting students choose their own books and by creating quiet reading periods.

4Parents also have an influence. Children who see adults reading at home are more likely to pick up the habit themselves.

(Adapted from an education magazine)

exercises.passage:
1City dwellers frequently feel disconnected from nature. Concrete streets, noise and pollution can cause stress, while a few minutes in a park can have the opposite effect.

2Research has shown that spending time in green areas lowers blood pressure and improves mood. Children who play outdoors tend to be more active and creative, and elderly people who walk in parks maintain better mobility.

3Green spaces also benefit the environment. Trees absorb carbon dioxide and provide shade, while grass and soil soak up rainwater, reducing the risk of floods. Parks provide habitats for birds and insects, helping to safeguard biodiversity.

4To make green spaces accessible, planners are designing neighbourhoods so that every home is within a short walk of a park. Community gardens, where residents grow vegetables together, are another way to bring nature into the city.

(Adapted from an urban-planning magazine)

Community groups can help by organising tree-planting days and cleaning up neglected corners. Even a small garden on a balcony or a roof can bring colour, shade and fresh air into crowded neighbourhoods.

The tourism industry is growing fast and offers many job opportunities 20 young people. Graduates can work in hotels, travel agencies or restaurants.

The industry is growing so fast that numerous hotels and travel companies report difficulty finding enough qualified staff. Young people with good language skills and a friendly personality are therefore in great demand.

Skills you need

Employers look for staff 21 speak at least one foreign language and enjoy meeting people. Being polite and patient is 22 important.

Training

Our college provides practical courses in which students 23 real guests during internships. After finishing the course, 24 can easily find work in well-known hotels. 25 today for more information.

Our college has strong links with leading hotel chains in several cities, and countless graduates are offered positions before they have even finished their studies. The next course begins in September, and applications are now open.

a. Guest: Hello, I have a reservation under the name Nguyen.

c. Many students have decided to start their own projects.

d. We hope you can visit us again.

Yours sincerely, Hoa

b. Old phones and computers contain harmful chemicals.

c. If they are thrown away carelessly, these chemicals pollute soil and water.

d. Proper recycling is therefore essential.

a. Parks bring many benefits to city dwellers.

b. They provide space for exercise and relaxation.

c. They also help to keep the air clean.

d. More parks should therefore be built.

exercises.title: Câu 31–40 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Electronic waste, or e-waste, includes discarded phones, computers, televisions and other devices. [II] It is the fastest-growing category of household rubbish in the world, with millions of tonnes produced each year. [III] Short product lifespans and constant upgrades are the main reasons. [IV]

2E-waste contains valuable materials such as gold, silver and copper, but also toxic substances such as lead and mercury. When devices are burned or dumped, these chemicals can contaminate air, soil and water, putting the health of nearby residents at serious risk.

3Numerous countries still lack proper recycling systems, and a large share of e-waste is shipped to developing nations, where workers dismantle it by hand without protection. Some manufacturers have introduced take-back schemes, allowing customers to return old devices.

4Consumers can help by repairing devices instead of replacing them, donating working equipment and using official collection points. Extending the life of a phone by even one year can significantly reduce its environmental impact.

(Adapted from a technology report)

WOMEN IN STEM

Science, technology, engineering and mathematics offer exciting careers. 1. Women have made remarkable discoveries but are frequently less visible than men.

Role models can play a powerful part in changing this situation. When girls read about female astronauts, programmers and engineers, they begin to see these careers as realistic possibilities for themselves.

Several factors 2 girls from choosing STEM subjects, such as stereotypes and a lack of role models. 3.

Programmes that provide mentors and scholarships 4. When girls see successful women in these fields, they 5.

Some companies have also started to offer internships and training programmes specifically for women. These initiatives help to create a more balanced workforce and bring fresh ideas to fields that have long been dominated by men.

exercises.passage:
Smart Homes

A smart home uses connected devices that can be controlled by phone or voice. Lights, heating and security cameras can 6 automatically.

Voice assistants have become one of the most popular features of modern homes. Residents can ask them to play music, set an alarm or turn off the lights, which is particularly helpful for elderly people or those with limited mobility.

These systems help families 7 energy. For instance, a thermostat learns your habits and lowers the temperature when nobody is at home. 8, smart locks make houses safer.

Nevertheless, there are drawbacks. Smart devices are still costly, and they 9 be hacked if passwords are weak. 10 buying a system, make sure that it is secure. 11 careful, you can enjoy a more comfortable home.

As prices fall and devices become easier to use, the number of smart homes is expected to rise steadily. Experts predict that within a decade, many new houses will come with these systems already installed.

exercises.passage:
Science Club for Girls

Do you love science and technology? Our club encourages girls 12 explore careers in STEM fields through hands-on projects.

Our members have built solar-powered lamps, designed simple video games and visited a local science museum, where they met female researchers who explained their work. Numerous girls say that these experiences made them braver about trying difficult subjects.

Activities

Every week, members 13 experiments, build simple robots and meet women scientists. Last year, our team won 14 prize at the national robotics contest.

Join us

The club is open to girls aged 12 to 15. Membership is free, 15 places are limited. 16 you are curious, we would love to meet you! Register 17 the school office.

The club meets after school every Thursday in the science laboratory. Our teachers will provide all the materials, and members are encouraged to bring ideas for projects they would like to carry out together.

exercises.title: Câu 23–30 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 23–30).
exercises.passage:
1National parks and nature reserves protect areas of natural beauty and the wildlife that lives there. In Viet Nam, places such as Cuc Phuong and Cat Tien shelter rare species, including primates and tropical birds.

2Protected areas serve several purposes. They preserve biodiversity, safeguard water sources and offer opportunities for research and education. Moreover, they attract visitors, whose spending supports local economies.

3However, managing reserves is not simple. Illegal logging and hunting still occur, and increasing numbers of tourists can disturb animals. Rangers must therefore patrol large areas, frequently with limited resources.

4Many reserves now involve neighbouring communities, providing them with jobs as guides or rangers. When local people share the benefits, they are more willing to protect the forest.

(Adapted from a conservation report)
exercises.tr: Khu bảo tồn bảo vệ đa dạng sinh học, nguồn nước, thu hút du khách; khó quản lý; cần cộng đồng tham gia.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Smart homes are becoming increasingly common around the world. [II] These houses contain devices that communicate with each other through the internet. [III] A homeowner can, For instance, switch on the air conditioner while still on the way home. [IV]

2Energy management is one of the biggest benefits. Sensors detect when rooms are empty and turn off lights automatically, while smart meters show exactly how much electricity each appliance uses. Over time, families can cut their bills by a significant amount.

3Safety is another advantage. Cameras and door sensors send alerts to a phone if something unusual happens, and smoke detectors can warn residents even when they are away. For elderly people living alone, such systems provide reassurance to relatives.

4Nevertheless, there are concerns about privacy and cost. A connected device collects data about its users’ habits, and this information must be protected. Until prices fall and security enhances, numerous families may hesitate to adopt the technology.

(Adapted from a technology magazine)
exercises.tr: Nhà thông minh tiết kiệm năng lượng, an toàn, nhưng chi phí và quyền riêng tư là mối lo.

exercises.passage:
5G Networks

The fifth generation of mobile networks, known 1 5G, is much faster than 4G. A film that once took several minutes to download can now be received in seconds.

Telecommunications companies have already begun to install the new equipment in major cities. Because the signals travel over shorter distances, many more antennas are needed than for previous generations, and this makes the network costly to build.

This speed will 2 new technologies such as self-driving cars and remote surgery. Doctors will be able to operate on patients thousands of kilometres away, 3 saving lives in remote areas.

However, building 5G networks requires huge investment. 4, some people worry about its effects on health, although scientists have found no 5 evidence. 6 the doubts, the technology is spreading fast.

Nevertheless, users in rural areas may have to wait for several years before they enjoy the same speeds as those in substantial cities. Governments are therefore being urged to help fund networks in places where companies see little profit.

Disaster Relief Volunteers

After the recent floods in the central provinces, thousands of families need urgent help. We are looking 7 volunteers to join our relief team.

The floods destroyed more than five thousand homes and damaged roads, schools and clinics in numerous villages. Local authorities are working hard to provide emergency shelter, but the scale of the damage is greater than they can manage alone.

Your tasks

Volunteers will pack food, 8 clean water and help rebuild damaged homes. You do not need special skills, 9 you must be physically fit and ready to work in difficult conditions.

How to join

Please 10 the form on our website. Selected volunteers will be contacted 11 phone. Thank you in advance 12 your generosity.

If you cannot join us in person, you can still help by donating clothes, dry food or money. Every contribution, however small, will go directly to families in need, and a full report will be published on our website.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 13–20).
exercises.passage:
1Festival food is more than something to eat; it is a way of keeping traditions alive. Each dish carries a story about a community’s history, beliefs and relationship with nature.

2During Tet, banh chung wraps rice, beans and pork in leaves to symbolise the earth and gratitude to ancestors. At the Mid-Autumn Festival, round moon cakes represent family unity, and their fillings vary from region to region.

3Preparing these foods is frequently a family event. Grandparents teach younger relatives how to wrap, steam or bake, passing on techniques that are rarely written down. In this way, cooking becomes a lesson in culture as well as in skill.

4Today, many people purchase ready-made festival foods owing to their busy lives. While this is convenient, some worry that the personal connection will be lost. They encourage families to cook together at least once a year.

(Adapted from a cultural magazine)
exercises.tr: Món ăn lễ hội mang ý nghĩa văn hóa, truyền qua gia đình; ngày nay mua sẵn tiện nhưng mất gắn kết.

exercises.passage:
CLIMATE EDUCATION

Understanding climate change is essential for the next generation. 26. Yet numerous students learn about the subject only briefly.

Some schools have introduced projects in which students count the number of plastic bottles thrown away in a week and then suggest ways to reduce them. These practical activities make a global problem feel local and understandable.

Climate education should 27 both science and action. Students can measure their school’s energy use and 28.

Projects like these make learning practical. They 29 responsibility and demonstrate that individuals can make a difference. If schools give climate topics more time, students 30.

Teachers say that when students participate in such projects, they frequently influence their families as well. Children who learn to save energy at school frequently remind their parents to switch off lights and unplug chargers at home.

(Adapted from an education journal)

exercises.title: Câu 31–40 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 31–40).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Climate education is gaining importance in schools around the world. [II] Students learn why the planet is warming and what can be done about it. [III] Some countries have even made climate topics a compulsory part of the national curriculum. [IV]

2Effective climate education goes beyond textbooks. Field trips to wetlands, tree-planting days and energy-saving competitions give students first-hand experience. Such activities help them to see how everyday choices are linked to global challenges.

3Teachers, however, face challenges. Many have not received special training, and the subject crosses several disciplines, from geography to economics. Some also worry about presenting a worrying topic without making students anxious.

4Experts therefore recommend combining facts with positive action. When young people feel that their efforts matter, they are more likely to stay engaged and to inspire others.

(Adapted from an education report)
exercises.tr: Giáo dục khí hậu cần trải nghiệm thực tế, hỗ trợ giáo viên, kết hợp kiến thức và hành động tích cực.

Some countries 9 to keep older workers employed for longer. Families and neighbours can also help by 10.

Society will have to adapt in countless ways, from building homes that are suitable for elderly people to training more nurses and carers. At the same time, it is crucial to recognise that older citizens remain active and valuable members of the community.

The city health department is organising a free health check-up day for residents aged fifty and over. The event will be held at the community centre 11 Sunday, 6 December.

Last year, more than twelve hundred people attended the event, and several of them were advised to see a specialist after the tests revealed early signs of illness. Doctors stress that finding challenges early makes them easier to treat.

Services

Doctors will 12 blood pressure, test eyesight and give advice on healthy diets. Nurses will also 13 flu vaccinations to those who need them.

Notes

Please bring your ID card and any 14 medical records. No appointment is necessary, but 15 are advised to arrive early. 16 the venue is wheelchair-accessible, everyone is welcome.

Light refreshments will be provided, and volunteers will be on hand to help elderly visitors move between the different stations. If you cannot attend, please ask a relative or neighbour to take your place and share the information.

exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 17–24).
exercises.passage:
1Every year, millions of people move from the countryside to cities in search of better opportunities. Cities offer more jobs, better schools and modern hospitals, which attract families and young workers alike.

2However, rapid migration creates pressure on urban areas. Housing becomes expensive, public transport is crowded and many new arrivals end up living in informal settlements without basic services. Schools and hospitals may struggle to cope with demand.

3Rural communities also face consequences. When young adults leave, villages lose workers and farmland may be left unused. Older residents are frequently left behind without family support.

4To manage migration, experts suggest creating jobs outside substantial cities and improving rural services. If villages offered good schools, clinics and internet access, fewer people would feel forced to leave.

(Adapted from a social-studies textbook)

Mobile games are played by millions of people every day. They are easy to download and 25 to play in short breaks.

Game developers use clever techniques to keep players interested, such as daily rewards and short levels that are easy to finish. This design makes it challenging to stop playing, which is why so many people lose track of time.

Parents can help by learning about the games their children play and agreeing on sensible rules together. Playing together occasionally is also a good way to understand why a game is so attractive.

exercises.passage:
1[I] Regular health check-ups are one of the simplest ways to safeguard your well-being. [II] Numerous illnesses, such as diabetes and high blood pressure, develop slowly and show no obvious symptoms in the early stages. [III] A routine examination can detect them before they become serious. [IV]

2Doctors recommend that adults have a general check-up at least once a year. During the visit, they measure weight and blood pressure, take blood samples and ask about lifestyle habits such as diet, exercise and sleep. Based on the results, they can give tailored advice.

3Despite these benefits, many people avoid check-ups. Some fear bad news, others believe they are too busy or that they feel perfectly healthy. In addition, the cost of tests can be a barrier for low-income families.

4To address this, some employers and local governments organise free screening days. Making check-ups easier and cheaper is likely to encourage more people to take care of their health before problems appear.

(Adapted from a healthcare website)

exercises.title: Câu 7–11 · Sắp xếp câu
exercises.instruction: Chọn phương án sắp xếp các câu/lời thoại thành một đoạn hội thoại hoặc đoạn văn hợp lý (câu 7–11).
exercises.passage:
Câu 7

a. Counsellor: What subjects do you enjoy most at school?

b. Student: I like biology and chemistry.

c. Counsellor: Have you considered studying medicine?

d. Student: Yes, but I’m worried about the long years of study.

Câu 8

a. Trang: Which career are you thinking about?

b. Long: I’d like to become a software engineer.

c. Trang: That requires strong maths skills, doesn’t it?

d. Long: Yes, so I’m taking extra classes.

Câu 9

Dear Sir or Madam,

a. I am writing to enquire about the English course for adults that you advertised.

b. Could you tell me when the next course starts?

c. I would also like to know how much it costs.

d. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully, Vy

Câu 10

a. Digital literacy is the ability to use technology safely and effectively.

b. It includes searching for reliable information and protecting personal data.

c. In the modern workplace, these skills are as important as reading and writing.

d. Schools should therefore teach them from an early age.

Câu 11

a. Choosing a career is a major decision.

b. It should be based on your interests and strengths.

c. Talking to professionals can give you a realistic picture of the job.

d. Finally, remember that careers can change over time.

exercises.instruction: Đọc đoạn văn rồi chọn phương án phù hợp nhất cho từng chỗ trống đánh số (câu 12–16).
exercises.passage:
DIGITAL LITERACY

In today’s world, knowing how to use technology is as crucial as reading. 12. People who are digitally literate can find reliable information and avoid online scams.

Digital skills are especially vital for young people who will soon enter the workforce. Employers increasingly expect new staff to use spreadsheets, collaborate online and recognise suspicious emails without special training.

Digital literacy also includes 13 and respecting other people’s rights online. Numerous schools 14 lessons on these topics.

Adults need to keep learning as well, because software and apps 15. Libraries and community centres frequently 16.

However, digital literacy is not only about technical skills. It also involves thinking critically about the information we find online and asking who produced it, why it was produced and whether it can be trusted.

(Adapted from an education website)

exercises.instruction: Đọc đoạn văn rồi chọn phương án phù hợp nhất cho từng chỗ trống đánh số (câu 17–22).
exercises.passage:
Biodiversity

Biodiversity refers to the variety of living things on Earth, from tiny insects to huge whales. A healthy ecosystem 17 many different species, each playing a role.

Scientists have identified about two million species, but they believe that numerous millions more remain unknown, especially in tropical forests and the deep sea. Every year, some of them disappear before they are even described.

Unfortunately, human activities are 18 this balance. Deforestation, pollution and overfishing have caused hundreds of species to disappear. 19 one species disappears, others that depend on it may also suffer.

Protecting biodiversity benefits people too. Forests provide clean air and water, and insects 20 crops. 21 conservation, we can save countless species from extinction. 22 we protect nature now, future generations will enjoy it.

Protecting biodiversity is therefore not a luxury but a necessity. Governments, businesses and ordinary citizens all have a part to play, from creating protected areas to choosing products that do not harm wildlife.

exercises.title: Câu 23–32 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 23–32).
exercises.passage:
1[I] Cultural exchange programmes bring together young people from different countries to live, study and work side by side. [II] Participants typically stay with host families, attend local schools and join community activities. [III] Through daily contact, they learn about each other’s customs, languages and ways of thinking. [IV]

2The benefits are substantial. Participants improve their language skills far more rapidly than in a classroom, and they develop confidence in tackling unfamiliar situations. Many also form friendships that last for decades, creating a global network of contacts.

3Host communities gain as well. Families learn about other cultures without leaving home, and local students are inspired to study foreign languages or consider studying abroad. Schools frequently report a more open and tolerant atmosphere after hosting exchange students.

4Challenges do exist, including homesickness, misunderstandings and the cost of travel. Good preparation and support from organisers can minimise these challenges. Ultimately, the understanding gained through such programmes helps to build a more peaceful and cooperative world.

(Adapted from a cultural-exchange brochure)
exercises.tr: Trao đổi văn hóa giúp học ngôn ngữ, tự tin, bạn bè; cộng đồng chủ nhà cũng hưởng lợi; thách thức có thể giảm nhờ chuẩn bị.

exercises.title: Câu 33–40 · Đọc hiểu
exercises.instruction: Đọc bài đọc rồi chọn đáp án đúng nhất cho mỗi câu hỏi (câu 33–40).
exercises.passage:
1Choosing a career is one of the biggest decisions a young person makes. It affects not only income but also happiness, because people who enjoy their work are generally more satisfied with life.

2The first step is self-assessment: identify your interests, strengths and values. Do you prefer working with people, numbers or ideas? Online tests and conversations with teachers can help you clarify these questions.

3Next, research possible careers. Discover what qualifications are required, what the working conditions are like and how the job market may change. Speaking to professionals or doing a short internship gives a realistic view of daily tasks.

4Finally, stay flexible. Many people change careers several times, and skills such as communication and problem-solving are useful in any field. A first choice does not have to be a final one.

(Adapted from a careers guide)
exercises.tr: Chọn nghề: hiểu bản thân, tìm hiểu nghề, thực tập, linh hoạt.
